title: W4 gate ordering and continuation recovery
description: Acquire the ApplicationMutationGate lease as new_run/restore BEFORE issuing the transaction root or preparing an allocation candidate and hold it across the window (currently taken inside _run_participant_transaction, after the root is minted, intent committed, and allocation durably committed). Implement the forward-resume reconcile_startup actually requires: reacquire the owner implied by kind, recompute the deterministic allocation candidate, advance through participants_applying/participants_applied/completed, persist the typed failure diagnostic, and latch a fatal when recovery cannot be proven. Wire the abort/failure half (_advance_intent_to_abort, STAGE_ABORTED, _validate_failure, _apply_recovery_diagnostic, _replay_failure are all unreachable) so _rollback_transaction records failure and a failed transaction cannot strand a permanent record. ACCEPTANCE: tests proving a crash at each boundary RESUMES rather than merely reporting ok, and that a failed New Run leaves no unresolvable journal entry. Resolves B-C1 through B-C4.
close_reason: Fixed at d33816ee973cc4c39a0d2d87d216e8ccf1d7dc92. Lease is now acquired before the transaction root is minted or any allocation candidate prepared, and held across the window; reconcile_startup genuinely resumes forward (reacquires the owner, recomputes the allocation candidate, advances participants_applying -> participants_applied -> completed, persists typed failures, latches fatal when recovery cannot be proven); the abort path is reachable so a failed transaction reaches aborted with a typed failure and strands no record. Full suite 2054 tests, 2051 passing, 0 failing, 3 pending (baseline +7). All five crash boundaries proven to RESUME with assertions on journal completed plus live GameState.day, not merely on ok. Differential mutation proof: full revert 0/7, B-C1-only revert 5/7, B-C2/C4-only revert 2/7 - each fix's tests depend on it. DesktopContinuationOperationJournal.gd was untouched; its advance() state machine was already correct and only SaveManager orchestration was missing. SCOPE NOTE: _rollback_transaction still does not touch the journal on a FIRST-attempt live failure - the next reconciliation pass resolves it to completed/aborted/fatal instead. Also noted: FakeRestoreParticipant.gd has a permissive generic prepare() shape (left alone; unrelated suites depend on it) and the new tests use a locally-scoped shape-correct fake.

title: Plan-02 tail remediation: integration seams broken behind permissive test doubles
description:
Both whole-branch reviewers (2026-08-23) returned NOT READY on dwm-p2r.32's delivered work. Eight Criticals. ROOT CAUSE both reviewers independently identified: throughout the workstream the test doubles were MORE PERMISSIVE (publication ledger fake accepting kinds the real ledger rejects) or MORE CAPABLE (checkpoint fake implementing an idempotency/conflict law production lacks) than the production objects, so green suites certified behavior the shipped graph does not have. The suite is 2039/2042 green and the integration is still broken.

DESKTOP HALF (reviewer A):
A-C1 three of four production publishers cannot talk to the production publication ledger - DesktopPublicationLedger hardcodes KINDS minesweeper_round|shop_purchase|schedule_done and one uniform PUBLICATION_KEYS, but the frozen union is causal_sequence|action_source|board_fate with per-kind shapes; board-fate, shop and round publishers all send frozen kinds/shapes and DesktopActionReceipt has no receipt_id for the binding check. Bootstrap injects the same real ledger into all four. Fails AFTER the admission CAS, in the forward-only region.
A-C2 minesweeper_round departure fails at board-fate commit post-admission: the coordinator builds the departure request from the pre-completion board identity/revision, then commits the action source first, which adopts the NONE/identity-null/revision+1 projection into the shared board state; the fate port then re-checks the prepared pre-state against the changed live board and returns board_fate_conflict. Only the no_departure round path is covered by a real-port test.
A-C3 the consequence checkpoint tier is write-only: nothing in the tree reads desktop-consequence-checkpoint.json, and the stored ordinal-2 stage_candidate is a shape DesktopConsequenceState.validate rejects, so adding a reader would fail. No occupied-slot conflict law exists in the real SaveManagerCheckpointPort even though Task 8's ordinal safety rationale cites that law by name.

PERSISTENCE HALF (reviewer B):
B-C1 the ApplicationMutationGate lease is acquired AFTER the transaction root is issued and the identity allocation is durably committed, inverting the frozen law that requires acquiring new_run/restore BEFORE issuing the root; a busy or fatal-latched gate burns identity and strands the journal record.
B-C2 nothing resumes an incomplete continuation forward - reconcile_startup verifies and returns ok for every non-terminal stage without reacquiring the owner, recomputing the allocation candidate, advancing a stage, or latching fatal.
B-C3 SaveManager documents that a later reconciliation pass finishes a participants_applied operation; no such pass exists.
B-C4 the journal abort/failure half is unreachable from production, so each failed New Run burns an allocation AND appends a permanent unresolvable record - an unbounded durable leak compounding dwm-p2r.33.
B-C5 both sealed evidence documents carry red_green_command_records: [] and a dangling test_log_bindings path; the builder silently skips missing logs, the schema sets no minItems, and no test asserts non-emptiness, so --check reports OK forever.

Full finding text including Importants and Minors is in the SDD ledger at .godot/worktrees/dwm-p2r13-resealed/.superpowers/sdd/progress.md and in this session's review reports. Child beads carry the fix waves.

Failures are COLLECTED rather than thrown one at a time so a mutation campaign gets per-mutation attribution instead of whichever guard happened to fire first. WHY HEAD_NOT_SUBJECT MUST PRECEDE WORKTREE_NOT_CLEAN. The worktree is legitimately dirty while Task 3 is in progress. If cleanliness were checked first the HEAD test would pass today and change verdict after the commit. The ordering makes the fixture deterministic in both states.

THE CANONICAL JSON ORACLE, THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING OF THE SESSION. A command record sha256 covers the canonical bytes of the record with sha256 REMOVED, and those bytes are produced by GDScript CanonicalJsonWriter.gd. The runner is PowerShell, so one byte of drift makes every record hash in the sealed gate wrong. TWELVE COMMITTED EVIDENCE DOCUMENTS WERE VERIFIED THIS SESSION TO BE BYTE-EXACT OUTPUT OF THAT WRITER, so they are a free oracle needing no Godot process: schedule/gate.json, the four contracts/*.json, both handoff/*.json, the three dialogic/*.json, runtime/game_state_surface.json and runtime/save_manager_surface.json. The fixture asserts three of them round-trip byte-exactly. Explicitly NOT canonical and never to be used as the oracle: baseline.json, documentation/legacy_disposition.json, legacy/legacy_heading_inventory.v1.json, localization/*.json which carry no trailing LF at all, runtime/*_required_surface.json which are pretty printed, and tooling/codegraph_*.json - all PowerShell ConvertTo-Json insertion-order output.
THE SINGLE MOST LIKELY IMPLEMENTATION BUG IS PINNED ON ITS OWN: PowerShell Sort-Object is case-INSENSITIVE by default and would order a before Z, whereas canonical order is by UTF-8 byte and puts Z first. That mistake would leave the document superficially plausible while invalidating every hash.

SUITES vs EXECUTED_SUITES: SORT BOTH, AND WHY. EvidenceValidator compares them as ARRAYS so order matters, yet a -gdir command has no requested order at all. Order was never the law; set equality is, and that is the law commit 727051ca broke. For -gtest commands suites comes from argv; for -gdir commands discovery follows GUT own rule, addons/gut/gut.gd line 229 sets _file_prefix to test_, recursive only with -ginclude_subdirs. executed_suites for both is the exact standalone res:// path lines in the log, DEDUPED, because the trust run emitted 26 such lines for 24 distinct scripts. The wrapper own SUITE_NOT_EXECUTED guard reads -gtest only, so for -gdir runs this record-level comparison is the ONLY thing enforcing the law.

THE 72 REQUIREMENT IDS ARE DERIVED, NEVER HARDCODED. Computed mechanically exactly as Phase2RCloseoutInventory._expected_requirement_ids computes them, giving exactly 72. The fixture fails GATE_REQUIREMENTS_HARDCODED if the literal req.audio.semantic_context appears anywhere in the runner source, and enforces coverage in BOTH directions: every derived id evidenced by at least one command, and no command claiming an id outside the derived set.

STEP 4 MANDATE IS PINNED BY A SOURCE-TEXT LAW. The fixture fails GATE_INVENTORY_OMITS_METADATA_SYNC unless the runner names tools/beads/Sync-Phase2RMetadata.ps1, because without it dwm-p2r.9 ten stale evidence links pinning 1abf65999f60e7fb reach Task 4 unchallenged.

title: W6a behavioral divergences: abandonment, failure caching, lease span, validators, progress shape
description: Split from W6 (dwm-p2r.35.6) - the items that are real behavioral bugs rather than comments/cosmetics. A-I7 DesktopConsequenceState.validate_recovery_payload enforces a 4-key action payload while the coordinator overwrites recovery_payload at ordinal 1 with a 21-key admission-ready payload, so the public static REJECTS the payload its own coordinator writes for the whole post-ordinal-1 life of every transaction - make it a discriminated union on payload_phase or delete it. A-I8 publication_progress ships {cursor, complete, callback_receipts} while the frozen shape is {publication_plan_sha256, callback_ids, next_callback_index, callback_receipts}, so the frozen plan-hash-mismatch rejection rule is unenforceable and a resumed coordinator cannot detect a cursor belonging to a different plan.

title: New Run cannot complete against the real Profile and Localization participants
description:
FOUND 2026-08-23 by Plan-02 Task 9's crash-recovery suite, the first test to drive start_new_run through the COMPLETE real production graph (every prior test - test_new_run_transaction.gd, test_save_manager.gd - wires fake participants for every key, which is why this was never caught).

THE DEFECT. SaveManager.start_new_run() hardcodes two of its eight participant plans as caller-independent literals that bypass .prepare() entirely: plans[profile] = {profile: {}} and plans[localization] = {} (autoload/SaveManager.gd around lines 393-394). ProfileSchema.validate({}) rejects the empty profile candidate (ProfileSchema.gd:87 requires an exact 7-key object) and LocalizationManager._is_restore_plan_valid({}) rejects the empty localization candidate (LocalizationManager.gd:391-392 requires four keys). Unconditional: no profile.json content changes it, because the literal plan never reads _profile. Confirmed live for the profile half (participant order run -> desktop_consequence -> desktop_board -> PROFILE -> localization -> ... means profile fails first every time); the localization half is confirmed by code reading since the loop never reaches it.

WHY IT WAS DISCLOSED NOT FIXED. The adjacent comment states the intent - an empty profile patch is meant to PRESERVE the complete global profile for a new game - but LocalizationRestoreParticipant.prepare needs an explicit locale_id and ProfileRestoreParticipant.prepare needs a legacy_profile_patch_input. Deciding what start_new_run should supply, including the no-prior-profile.json fresh-install case, is product/design work Plan 02's brief never specifies. Task 9 proved it fail-closed, documented it at the source, and asserted it in DesktopAmendmentEvidenceGit.honest_gaps() (covered by test_desktop_crash_recovery.gd) so it cannot regress silently.

ACCEPTANCE. Decide the starting profile/locale semantics for a new run (including fresh install with no profile.json), wire start_new_run to supply real prepared candidates instead of the two literals, and prove a New Run completes end to end through the real ProfileManager/LocalizationManager pair - not fakes.
design: PRODUCT DECISION (user, 2026-08-24, controller session): Option A on both axes. (1) STARTING PROFILE: a New Run PRESERVES the complete global profile (preferences, gallery unlocks, input mappings, visited lines). Implement by routing the live profile through the real participant seam: plans[profile] built from _restore_participants[profile].prepare with legacy_profile_patch_input = {} (empty dict). prepare_legacy_profile_patch({}, {}) returns the live profile unchanged when migration_receipts.legacy_game_state_profile_v1 is already true, and a defaults-merged validated 7-key candidate otherwise; fresh install (no profile.json) therefore starts from ProfileSchema defaults. (2) LOCALE: chained from the prepared profile candidate preferences.language exactly as the restore path does at SaveManager.gd:1044-1047 - the profile prep returns locale_id, feed it to _restore_participants[localization].prepare. Fresh install gets schema default en. NO new initial_context key; _validate_new_run_context and all callers unchanged. IMPLEMENTATION NOTES: the honest-gap comment block at SaveManager.gd:448-461 must go; DesktopAmendmentEvidenceGit.honest_gaps() asserts this gap and is republished inside the sealed amendment documents, so fixing it drifts the amendment family and PAYS FOR A RE-SEAL - extract the bound-path sets from all four sealed documents first (as dwm-p2r.34 did) to confirm coupling, and fold the parked dwm-p2r.37 into that same re-seal pair. test_desktop_crash_recovery.gd currently asserts the fail-closed defect and must flip to assert the working path. Acceptance unchanged: prove a New Run completes end to end against the REAL ProfileManager/LocalizationManager pair, not fakes, including the fresh-install case.
notes: ADDENDUM (user decision via AskUserQuestion, 2026-08-24, dwm-p2r.33 implementation session): a THIRD caller-independent literal was unblocked by the profile/localization fix - start_new_run passed initial_context audio_context straight into plans[audio] = {snapshot: ...} without routing it through AudioRestoreParticipant.prepare(). The frozen _validate_new_run_context contract requires audio_context to be EXACTLY {}, but AudioManager._validate_snapshot requires the exact 4-key shape (music_context_id/music_context/ambience_context_id/ambience_context), so no caller - including the real MenuScene - could complete a New Run through the complete real graph, and a persisted new-run snapshot carrying audio_context {} would be unrestorable at the real audio prep. DECISION: Option A - the frozen {} already means a new run starts with NO audio context; translate it once inside start_new_run into AudioManager's own canonical empty snapshot (all four keys, empty ids = no music, no ambience), build the persisted RunSnapshot with the translated shape (keeping new-run saves restorable), and route plans[audio] through the real audio participant with the prepared profile candidate preferences, mirroring the restore path. Validator, callers, and initial_context keys all stay unchanged. No new honest gap is disclosed for audio because it is fixed in the same change.

title: No production facade reaches complete_presentation_stage, so the only public completion door refuses every command
description:
FOUND BY the fresh-context review of the dwm-p2r.20 fix plan.

THE GAP. autoload/GameState.gd exposes complete_day_resolution_stage, which forwards to
DayResolutionCoordinator.complete_route_stage. There is NO facade anywhere in autoload/ for
complete_presentation_stage.

Combine that with two facts and the seam is closed end to end:
1. GameStateDayResolutionPort.begin_next_stage is the ONLY production producer of
   await_registered_command, and it enters that branch only when presentation_request is non-empty.
2. Since dadb8680a, complete_route_stage refuses exactly that with presentation_completion_required.

So the only publicly reachable completion door refuses every command production can generate, and
the door that could accept them has no public caller. No walk can settle a presentation today.

NOT A REGRESSION. complete_presentation_stage never had a production caller; the p2r18 notes record
that Plan 03 owns the Done dispatch. dadb8680a did not remove a working path - it closed a door that
was accepting the wrong receipts. This bead exists so the gap is tracked rather than rediscovered.

ACCEPTANCE. Either Plan 03 lands the Done dispatch that drives complete_presentation_stage, or a
facade is added and its ownership recorded. Whichever happens, an integration test proves a
committed-Schedule walk reaches a presentation, settles it, and advances - through public seams
only, with no test reaching into the coordinator directly.

title: complete_route_stage drops substage_id, so a substage is validated against the stage contract
description:
FOUND BY the fresh-context review of the dwm-p2r.14 route/presentation guard. Separate defect,
deliberately left out of that fix because it is a stage/substage confusion, not the
route/presentation one that fix was scoped to.

THE DEFECT. DayResolutionCoordinator.complete_route_stage builds the stage record it hands
_commit_completion as {stage_id, transaction_id} and drops substage_id, even though resume()
injects one into the command it registers. _commit_completion selects its validator on
str(stage.get(substage_id, )) != , so a substage arriving through the route door is validated
against STAGE_CONTRACTS[stage_id] instead of SUBSTAGE_CONTRACTS[kind].
complete_presentation_stage forwards substage_id correctly; only the route door drops it.
The pre-check in complete_route_stage has the same blind spot.

WHY IT MATTERS. It fails closed one way and OPEN the other. A substage envelope hits a kind
mismatch, fine. But a STAGE-level envelope for a substage transaction passes _validate_envelope,
and RunLifecycle.complete_active_stage skips _validate_owner_receipt when record kind is
substage, so the substage contract is bypassed end to end.

REACHABILITY. Surviving-date presentations ARE substages: GameStateDayResolutionPort
_presentation_site routes substage ids prefixed surviving_date: to a dating presentation.
complete_route_stage has no production caller today, and the dwm-p2r.14 guard now steers every
production-shaped awaiting command to the presentation door, which handles substage_id
correctly. So this is latent AND newly masked, which is precisely why it is filed rather than
left in a note.

ACCEPTANCE. complete_route_stage carries substage_id through to _commit_completion and to its own
pre-check, so a substage completion is validated against SUBSTAGE_CONTRACTS by kind through
either door. A RED test proves a stage-level envelope for a substage transaction is refused
before the fix and after it, rather than silently accepted. No change to the presentation door.

REFERENCE. docs/superpowers/notes/2026-08-20-p2r14-route-presentation-confusion.md, Honest limits.
close_reason: Fixed at 17ba4e174. complete_route_stage now forwards substage_id to _commit_completion, so a substage is validated against SUBSTAGE_CONTRACTS by kind through either door; the redundant pre-check was DELETED rather than repaired, because _commit_completion makes the same selection and makes it before any capture, so a second copy bought only the chance to disagree. Three tests added, all mutation-proven: dropping substage_id turns all three red, forcing the STAGE validator turns all three red, forcing the SUBSTAGE validator turns 25 red (top-level stages still answer to STAGE_CONTRACTS), and reading the id off _awaiting instead of the resolved command turns exactly the history test red. Root cause of the long survival: FakeDayResolutionStatePort.seed_playing_day declared a _schedule parameter and never read it, so every plan the unit suite ever built had zero substages; the parameter is now honoured, backward compatible at both call sites. Gates at the committed tree, all exit 0, no SUITE_NOT_EXECUTED: adapter 249/5282, Step 7.7 156/2101, guarded-path 77/3059, Step 8.8 164/1947 unchanged, doc tooling 24/1635 unchanged; every delta is the coordinator suite's own +3/+22. Sealed defect, stated as such: no production path reaches the fixed lines today because the whole route door is refused first. Honest limit recorded: the _launched_transaction clear in that function has zero cover before or after. Discovered and filed, not fixed: dwm-p2r.21 and dwm-p2r.22. Note: docs/superpowers/notes/2026-08-20-p2r20-substage-contract-through-the-route-door.md

comments.author: Siuuuers
comments.text:
FIXED AT 17ba4e174 (parent dadb8680a). Nothing pushed. dwm-p2r.14, .18 and .19 remain open.

THE DEFECT, BOTH DIRECTIONS. complete_route_stage read stage_id off the resolved command and nothing
else. A substage command carries its PARENT stage_id (resume adds substage_id as an extra key rather
than replacing it), so the pre-check validated a substage against STAGE_CONTRACTS[parent] and the
record handed to _commit_completion had no substage_id for its selector to fire on.
- Failed closed: a legitimate schedule_entry_complete envelope died on kind mismatch.
- Failed OPEN: the parent aggregate envelope PASSED, and RunLifecycle.complete_active_stage skips
  _validate_owner_receipt entirely when record kind is substage, trusting this caller to have picked
  the table. So a substage completed here met NO contract check at all and persisted whatever bytes
  it was handed.

THE FIX DELETES CODE RATHER THAN ADDING IT. My plan was to mirror the selection in the pre-check.
The cold review rejected that on a fact I had wrong: _commit_completion makes the same selection and
makes it BEFORE it captures anything (validates at :563-565, first capture at :566). So the
pre-check bought no earlier refusal, no different bytes and no different call log - only the chance
for two copies to disagree, which is what this bug was. Pre-check deleted; the record gains
substage_id, read off the RESOLVED command so the _registered_history path answers the same way.
Note this is the OPPOSITE disposition to the one I took an hour earlier on dwm-p2r.14, where I
declined a shared-predicate extraction on scope grounds. The difference is real: that would have
ADDED an abstraction, this REMOVES a duplicate that had already produced a defect.

REACHABILITY, CORRECTED. My first framing said a surviving_date substage always carries a
presentation_request. Not true - a superseded date has an empty site and completes immediately. The
correct and stronger claim: GameStateDayResolutionPort.begin_next_stage is the only production
producer of await_registered_command and enters that branch only when presentation_request is
non-empty, so since dadb8680a the WHOLE door is sealed, not just its substage path. This is a
sealed-defect fix guarding the door against its next caller.

WHY IT SURVIVED. FakeDayResolutionStatePort.seed_playing_day declared its third parameter _schedule
and never read it; begin_or_resume hardcoded {entries: []}. EVERY plan the unit suite has ever built
had zero substages, so the coordinator substage branches were structurally unreachable from it. The
parameter is now honoured - backward compatible, both pre-existing call sites pass []. Three further
fake corrections so it stops modelling what production does not do: both the await and the
complete_immediately branches now return a substage-kind envelope instead of the parent aggregate
(the complete_immediately half was missed on my first pass and caught by the review); and
_substage_receipt derives entry_receipt_id from the substage id as production does, so a test can
tell an implementation that routes one entry receipt to another entry substage.

RED FIRST, AND ONE RED RUN REJECTED. Observed 30 tests, 27 passing, exactly the 3 new red, 294/305.
An earlier RED run errored - the persisted-receipt assertion cast a null receipt to Dictionary - and
was not accepted as RED; the helper was made cast-safe and RED re-observed clean with zero script
errors.

MUTATIONS, each proving a different claim, all reverted. Suite alone 27/283 before, 30/305 after.
  drop substage_id from the _commit_completion record  -> 27/30, 3 red (all new), 294/305
  _commit_completion always uses the STAGE validator   -> 27/30, 3 red, 294/305
  _commit_completion always uses the SUBSTAGE validator-> 5/30, 25 red, 196/253: top-level stages
                                                          still answer to STAGE_CONTRACTS
  read substage_id off _awaiting, not the command      -> 29/30, ONE red, and it is the history test
  delete _launched_transaction =                       -> 30/30 ALL GREEN, reported not hidden
The fourth is the one that matters. The review PREDICTED it would stay green and recommended a
history test; that test was added and is now the only thing the mutation turns red. Reviewing the RED
before writing the production line is what bought that.

OBSERVED GATES, baselines at dadb8680a. All exit 0, no SUITE_NOT_EXECUTED, orphans 24.
  hospital_dating_adapter_gate (18)   246/5260 -> 249/5282  (+3/+22)
  Step 7.7 hospital_order_green (11)  153/2079 -> 156/2101  (+3/+22)
  guarded-path regression (5)          74/3037 ->  77/3059  (+3/+22)
  Step 8.8 presentation_day7 (12)     164/1947 -> 164/1947  unchanged; RUN, not assumed
  doc tooling (5)                      24/1635 ->  24/1635  unchanged
Deleting the pre-check changed no existing test, which the review predicted and is now observed.

HONEST LIMIT. _launched_transaction = in this function has zero cover before and after; deleting it
leaves everything green. Unreachable on every existing path. Left alone as pre-existing, but nobody
should call it proven.

DISCOVERED AND FILED, NOT FIXED: dwm-p2r.21 (no production facade reaches
complete_presentation_stage, so the only public completion door refuses every command) and
dwm-p2r.22 (a replayed substage completion never reports duplicate_transaction).

title: Prove the Hospital condition flag is checkpointed with the plan it belongs to
description:
RE-SCOPED on 2026-08-19. This bead was filed as a schema change and is now ONE TEST. The
original premise was wrong; see the 04:47 correction comment for the full withdrawal.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOW. Prove, rather than argue, that the Hospital condition flag and the
resolution plan are checkpointed and restored TOGETHER, so a resumed walk re-derives the same
P01.presentation.intent it already published.

WHY THE ORIGINAL PREMISE FAILED. The bead claimed a restore could produce a plan sitting
mid-Hospital beside a cleared pending_hospital, because _hospital_site() reads
should_route_hospital() live and resume() never re-runs begin_or_resume. It cannot. Both halves
come from the same bytes:

  * pending_hospital is a member of GameState._SAVE_WHITELIST.
  * capture_run_snapshot_input() builds gameplay from that whitelist and returns it beside
    lifecycle, which carries active_resolution_plan, in ONE dictionary.
  * GameStateDayResolutionPort._checkpoint_inputs() hands that one dictionary to
    RunSnapshotSchema.build, whose GAMEPLAY_FIELDS lists pending_hospital, producing ONE document.
  * GameState._apply_run_snapshot_silent() puts the lifecycle, the gameplay bag (through the same
    whitelist), the Contacts index and the committed aggregate back from that one document.

So persisting the derived required would have added a PLAN_KEYS member, from_dict validation, a
RunSnapshotSchema member and a migration branch to defend against a state the system cannot reach.
Neither Option A nor Option B is to be built.

THE REAL GAP, WHICH THIS BEAD CLOSES. Nothing asserted that atomicity. The safety of the resume
path rests on pending_hospital staying in _SAVE_WHITELIST and in RunSnapshotSchema's gameplay set,
and RunSnapshotSchema's gameplay check is an ALLOWLIST that rejects unknown members and says
nothing about a member that went missing. Every existing cut in
tests/integration/test_committed_schedule_presentation_resume.gd restores from an in-memory
to_dict() and leaves the flag SET across the cut, so all of them would pass just as happily if the
flag stopped being captured at all.

ACCEPTANCE. One test in tests/integration/test_committed_schedule_presentation_resume.gd that
crashes across the Hospital presentation, rebuilds the process from the ON-DISK checkpoint, and
proves the restored pending_hospital and the restored plan came back together -- so the intent
re-derives byte-identically BECAUSE the flag travelled with the plan rather than by luck. No
schema change, no new PLAN_KEYS member, and no DEVIATION-7.

NO LONGER BLOCKS dwm-p2r.15. The blocking edge was added on the withdrawn premise: a missing test
is not a reason to refuse to seal evidence, whereas an unfixed corruption was. Edge removed
2026-08-19.

DO NOT, STILL. Do not fix anything here by holding the answer in memory on the port, and do not
re-read live state anywhere on the resume path.
acceptance_criteria: Proved rather than argued: pending_hospital and active_resolution_plan are checkpointed and restored TOGETHER, so a resumed walk re-derives the same P01.presentation.intent it already published. One test in tests/integration/test_committed_schedule_presentation_resume.gd crashes across the Hospital presentation, rebuilds the process owners, and restores through the production _apply_run_snapshot_silent seam from ONE on-disk document; the rebuilt process starts with the flag cleared by reset_game(), so pending_hospital and the plan can come back only from those bytes, and both halves are asserted against the document itself. SCOPE OF THE CRASH, stated exactly rather than as "bytes only" (corrected 2026-08-20 after cold review): the FakeDesktopConsequenceSource condition and board-fate memos ARE deliberately carried across, modelling the per-causal-day durability Plan 02 owns, because DEVIATION-6 re-derives Hospital miss ids from the condition receipt and a fresh receipt would move the intent for reasons unrelated to pending_hospital; and the schedule registry plus its fingerprint are loaded once in before_each rather than rebuilt. Neither carries pending_hospital nor the plan, so neither weakens what this test catches. Mutation-proved on both halves: dropping pending_hospital from GameState._SAVE_WHITELIST, or from RunSnapshotSchema.GAMEPLAY_FIELDS, must turn exactly this test red and name the cause. NO schema change, NO new PLAN_KEYS member, and NO DEVIATION-7. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19 by the 04:47 correction comment: the earlier criteria demanded a persisted derivation-time answer recorded as a numbered DEVIATION, and that premise was withdrawn -- neither Option A nor Option B is to be built. Do not fix anything here by holding the answer in memory on the port, and do not re-read live state anywhere on the resume path.

comments.author: Siuuuers
comments.text:
DECISION: OPTION A. Persist the derivation-time answer in Plan 01.

Option B is not rejected -- it is SEQUENCED AFTER A. See "they are not competitors" below.

WHO DECIDED. The bead was filed with both options costed and neither chosen, because the choice
looked like a maintainer scope call. The maintainer then explicitly delegated it. Recorded here so
the decision has an owner and a date rather than appearing as a fait accompli in a diff.

WHY NOT B, TODAY

B is not a trade-off against A right now; it is a regression. The desktop-consequence source is
DELIBERATELY unconfigured in production (DEVIATION-5), so binding `required` to the condition
receipt would make every ordinary no-Hospital day fail closed at hospital_if_triggered -- today the
stage answers immediately from the live flag and never touches that seam. Plan 01 line 1303 also
forbids this plan from building the desktop side, and dwm-p2r.9's DesktopConditionPolicyPort was
never authored (DEVIATION-2). So choosing B means dwm-p2r.15 waits on a plan that has not started.

WHY A, AND WHY IT IS CHEAPER THAN THIS BEAD ASSUMED

The bead priced A as the DEVIATION-4 blast radius. Measured at ed29271f rather than assumed:

• Every test JSON fixture that carries `active_resolution_plan` -- 13 files -- carries it NULL.
  A new plan member touches ZERO fixtures. (An earlier comment on dwm-p2r.18 said 17; the count
  differs, the substance does not: there are no non-null occurrences anywhere under tests/.)
• SaveMigrations.gd:80-91 ALREADY contains the worked precedent, added by this bead's own earlier
  commit for command_id / resolution_issuer_receipt / day_resolution_start_receipt: a legacy save
  caught mid-resolution gets the members it genuinely had, and fabricating ancestry no issuer
  anchored is explicitly refused. A fourth member follows that exact pattern.
• So the real cost is PLAN_KEYS + from_dict validation + RunSnapshotSchema + one migration branch,
  with a three-member precedent landed and green.

A is also the CONSISTENT choice rather than a new idea. The plan persists the resolution root and
the start receipt for exactly one reason: resume() never re-runs begin_or_resume, so a restore must
derive the SAME children it already published. `required` is the last live-sourced input to that
derivation. Putting it in the same persisted bundle finishes the decision this bead's parent
already made; leaving it out is the inconsistency.

THEY ARE NOT COMPETITORS

A owns WHERE the answer lives. B owns WHERE THE ANSWER COMES FROM. When Plan 02 lands its
DesktopConditionPolicyPort, the persisted member stays exactly as A leaves it and only its SOURCE
changes -- from the live should_route_hospital() flag to the anchored condition receipt. Choosing A
now does not have to be undone by B later, which is what makes it safe to choose now rather than
waiting.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS

• Persist the DERIVATION-TIME answer, written when the Hospital stage first derives and read by
  every later derivation, including after a restore. Do not re-read live state anywhere on the
  resume path.
• Bool vs small record is left to the implementer, with one constraint: `_derive_hospital_rows`
  RE-RESOLVES the condition receipt through the consequence source on the same path, so whatever is
  persisted must not be able to disagree with that receipt. If the two can drift, persist enough to
  make the disagreement detectable and fail closed; if they cannot, a bool is sufficient. Decide
  that by reading the resume path, not by guessing.
• Write the red test FIRST: a Step 8.2 crash cut with pending_hospital CLEARED in the restored
  process. test_committed_schedule_presentation_resume.gd leaves the flag set across every existing
  cut, which is precisely why this was invisible.
• Record the result as DEVIATION-7 in docs/superpowers/notes/2026-08-18-p2r18-review-brief.md,
  alongside 4, 5 and 6, per this bead's acceptance criteria.
• The DO NOT in the description still stands: never fix this by holding the answer in memory on the
  port.

comments.text:

WHAT I CLAIMED

"On resume the port re-runs `_presentation_site()`, another LIVE read of should_route_hospital().
If the flag is clear when the process comes back, the resumed walk derives no presentation for a
stage that already published an intent." I treated the flag as process-local state that a restore
could lose.

WHY IT CANNOT HAPPEN

`pending_hospital` is DURABLE, and it is checkpointed in the same bundle as the plan:

• autoload/GameState.gd:89 -- `pending_hospital` is a member of `_SAVE_WHITELIST`.
• GameState.capture_run_snapshot_input() (:2067) builds `gameplay` from that whitelist and returns
  it alongside `lifecycle` (which carries `active_resolution_plan`) in ONE dictionary.
• GameStateDayResolutionPort.prepare_completion -> _prepared() (:520) hands exactly that bundle to
  the coordinator as `snapshot_input`, which DayResolutionCoordinator (:429) forwards verbatim to
  the checkpoint port. So EVERY stage-completion checkpoint records the plan and the flag together.
• RunSnapshotSchema:52 lists `pending_hospital` in the validated gameplay member set, so it is not
  dropped in transit.
• GameState.restore_live_run_state (:2048) applies `gameplay` back through apply_save_dict().

So the plan and the flag are captured atomically and restored atomically. The state I described --
a restored plan sitting mid-Hospital next to a cleared flag -- cannot be produced by the checkpoint
path, because both halves come from the same bytes. Restoring an OLDER save does not help the bug
either: it restores an older plan with it, which is consistent again.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE OPTION A/B DECISION RECORDED ABOVE

It is moot, and should not be acted on. Persisting the derived `required` would have added a member
to PLAN_KEYS, from_dict validation, RunSnapshotSchema and a migration branch to defend against a
state the system cannot reach. The reasoning in that comment about A vs B still holds IF the
premise had held; the premise did not. I am leaving the decision comment in place rather than
deleting it, so the record shows what was decided and why it was withdrawn.

WHAT WAS STILL WORTH SOMETHING

dwm-p2r.18 Finding 4 -- the PRESENTATION window -- was real and is fixed (commit 0dea588e). That
one did not depend on durability: both reads happened inside one live process with a physical
presentation between them, and the test drives exactly that.

And one real gap survives, which is the only thing I would keep this bead open for:

NOTHING PROVES THE ATOMICITY THIS ARGUMENT RESTS ON. The safety of the resume path now depends on
`pending_hospital` staying in `_SAVE_WHITELIST` and in RunSnapshotSchema's gameplay set. No test
asserts that the flag and the plan survive a crash cut TOGETHER; the resume suite leaves the flag
set across every cut and never varies it, so it would pass just as happily if the flag stopped
being captured at all. A future change that moved `pending_hospital` out of the whitelist -- or a
new condition input that is never captured -- would silently reintroduce exactly the corruption I
described, with no test objecting.

RECOMMENDED RE-SCOPE (needs a maintainer nod, since I am the one who got this wrong and a negative
deserves a second reader)

Reduce this bead from a schema change to one test in
tests/integration/test_committed_schedule_presentation_resume.gd: crash across the Hospital
presentation, rebuild the process from the on-disk checkpoint, and assert that the restored
`pending_hospital` and the restored plan agree -- i.e. that the intent re-derives byte-identically
BECAUSE the flag came back with it, not by luck. That turns the argument above into a guarantee and
costs a fraction of Option A.

If that re-scope is accepted, this bead should also stop blocking dwm-p2r.15: a missing test is not
a reason to refuse to seal evidence, whereas an unfixed corruption was. The dependency edge I added
to .15 was added on the wrong premise and should come off with it.

title: Emit committed-Schedule presentation intents into the day-resolution walk
description:
Wire the committed-Schedule presentation PRODUCER: emit P01.presentation.intent into the
day-resolution walk so the Hospital/Dating adapters are actually launched.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Plan 01 Task 8 (dwm-p2r.14, commit db7c290b) delivered the presentation LAYER --
DialogicPresentationOwnerAdapter, HospitalPresentationPort, DatingPresentationPort, the trusted
DialogicBridge completion, port-only Hospital/Dating scenes, SceneRouter injection, coordinator
seam, and Bootstrap composition -- all proved by 161 tests. But nothing yet HANDS those ports a
command during a resolution, so no stage pauses on a presentation and the coordinator's retained
completion is never checkpointed into a stage. dwm-p2r.14's acceptance criteria require the adapters
to LAUNCH registered semantic routes; until this lands, they cannot.

CONFIRMED DEAD, NOT BROKEN. SceneRouter.goto_hospital(), goto_dating_entries() and
finish_current_dating_and_route() have ZERO callers, and GameState.apply_hospital_recovery_and_
advance_day() (autoload/GameState.gd:1271) now has zero callers too. Task 8 did not remove a working
path -- the Hospital scene was already unreachable. This bead is what makes it reachable for the
first time. Those four seams are left in place deliberately (Plan 03 / dwm-oyo may claim them);
they are flagged here rather than deleted.

WHY IT WAS SPLIT OUT (DEVIATION-4 on dwm-p2r.14, user-approved). Doing this correctly requires
persisting the resolution ROOT receipt in the plan, so a crash reconstructs the SAME intent and
completion children on restore. DayResolutionPlan.PLAN_KEYS is an EXACT member set with no
resolution_issuer_receipt, so adding it changes the persisted plan shape and ripples into
RunSnapshotSchema and SaveDocument v3. Holding the root in memory instead would work until the first
crash and then silently derive DIFFERENT children on restore -- a corruption that only surfaces on
reload, which is the worst shape this class of bug can have.

SCOPE
  * add resolution_issuer_receipt to DayResolutionPlan.PLAN_KEYS, create() and from_dict()
  * mint the resolution root and drive the RETAINED DayResolutionStartPort from
    GameStateDayResolutionPort.begin_or_resume (the start port still has no production caller;
    tests/integration/test_committed_schedule_day_resolution.gd:15 records that)
  * derive P01.presentation.intent for Hospital, each surviving date, and the deferred pair, plus
    the matching P01.presentation.completion, and return mode=await_registered_command
  * have DayResolutionCoordinator checkpoint the published completion receipt and advance the stage
    ONLY after that checkpoint succeeds (the retained-completion fields already exist)
  * SceneRouter.route_presentation() already exists and is tested; wire the walk to it
  * re-baseline RunSnapshotSchema, SaveDocument v3, save migrations + snapshot fixtures, and the
    plan / durability / committed-schedule suites
  * write the Plan 01 Step 8.2 resume suite: crash before intent derivation, after the exact intent,
    after route command, after physical completion signal, after exact completion derivation, after
    port validation, after domain receipt, and after stage checkpoint

ANCESTRY NOTE. The presentation ports already carry and project stage_id exactly as the producer
supplies it. Whether stage_id becomes a real issuer-derived P01.day_resolution.stage child (full
matrix fidelity) or stays DayResolutionPlan's synthetic string is a SEPARATE decision -- the ports do
not need it to change, and the approved DEVIATION-4 scope left it synthetic.

DO NOT. Edit DatingEndingRules, ENDING_PLAN_KEYS, the 11-ID interim manifest, playback, Gallery, or
the ending queue. dwm-oyo.6 owns the final ordered plan. DatingPresentationPort must stay
production-unconfigured; dwm-oyo.4 owns the relationship-board owner.
acceptance_criteria: A committed Hospital / surviving date / deferred pair produces an exact P01.presentation.intent and its matching P01.presentation.completion; the walk pauses on await_registered_command; the coordinator checkpoints the port's completion receipt before advancing the stage. The resolution root is persisted, so every crash cut in Plan 01 Step 8.2 restores the SAME intent and completion children and never replays a committed effect or renumbers a surviving presentation. RunSnapshotSchema, SaveDocument v3 and the save migrations accept and restore the new plan shape.

comments.text:
dwm-p2r.18 progress (uncommitted; working tree only). Base db7c290b.

SCOPE DECISION (user-approved this session) -- DEVIATION-5: the Plan-02 desktop-consequence
records arrive through a deliberately-unconfigured seam, and production fails closed.

The bead's scope bullet drive the RETAINED DayResolutionStartPort from begin_or_resume is
blocked on an input Plan 01 may not create. Two findings, same root cause:

* P01.presentation.intent projects P(day_resolution_start_receipt_id,...), so it REQUIRES the
  P01.day_resolution.start receipt. DayResolutionStartPort.gd:104-107 requires a board_fate_receipt
  with a nonblank receipt_id. Its only producer is Plan 02's DesktopBoardFatePort, which
  DEVIATION-2 established was never authored. Repo-wide grep: board_fate appears only in the
  issuer's closed child-kind list, the start port, the plan schema, and two test fixtures.
* P01.hospital.resolution projects P(condition_receipt_id,...), and its miss children are what
  the Hospital intent's input_receipt_ids name. Plan 01 has no condition receipt at all -- Hospital
  condition truth is GameState.should_route_hospital(), a bool with no receipt. That record is
  Plan 02's DesktopConditionPolicyPort output.

Plan 01 line 1303 forbids this plan from implementing desktop board fate, so neither can be built
here. User chose the configured-seam option: build the full producer, prove it over the real
substrate with the schema-exact fixture plan line 532 authorises, leave the seam unconfigured in
production, and let a stage that genuinely needs a presentation FAIL CLOSED naming the missing
input instead of silently skipping the presentation as it did before.

DONE

* PERSISTED RESOLUTION ROOT. DayResolutionPlan.PLAN_KEYS gains command_id,
  resolution_issuer_receipt and day_resolution_start_receipt. from_dict RE-PROVES the pair on every
  load: root purpose must be transaction_id, resolution_id must equal the root token (plan line
  560), the start receipt must exist exactly when the root does, must name this resolution, and
  must carry full provenance rather than an id. A tampered snapshot that keeps a well-shaped root
  under another token, drops the start receipt, or orphans it is refused rather than restored.
* IDEMPOTENCE MOVED TO THE COMMAND. resolution_id is now the issuer-minted token on the minted
  path, so RunLifecycle.begin_day_resolution / prepare_day_resolution key replay off command_id.
  Comparing tokens would have made every replayed Done command look like a new resolution and
  re-run a day that had already resolved.
* SAVE MIGRATION. The v1->v2 migration adds the three members to a legacy plan caught
  mid-resolution: command_id = its resolution_id, both receipts null. Faithful -- an old plan
  genuinely had no minted root; fabricating one would claim ancestry no issuer anchored. NOTE: all
  17 snapshot/save fixtures carry a NULL active_resolution_plan, so the SaveDocument v3 blast
  radius the bead feared did not materialise.
* THE PRODUCER. GameStateDayResolutionPort gains configure_resolution_identity(issuer, start_port)
  and configure_desktop_consequence_source(source), mints the root through issue(transaction_id),
  drives the retained start port's PURE prepare_from_committed_schedule, and persists both receipts
  into the plan. It derives, in the matrix's required order, P01.hospital.resolution ->
  P01.hospital.miss[] -> P01.presentation.intent -> P01.presentation.completion, and returns
  mode=await_registered_command so the walk PAUSES. Three variants land: Hospital (ordinal 0,
  hospital.faint), each surviving date (ordinal = index among surviving committed dates in slot
  order), and the deferred P-L pair (ordinal 0). Timeline locators are constructed then REQUIRED to
  be registered in DialogicTimelineCatalog. Derivation happens while the stage is still PENDING, so
  an undeliverable presentation leaves the run resumable rather than stranding an active stage.
* COORDINATOR. complete_presentation_stage() folds the port's completion receipt into the stage
  envelope, checkpoints the whole envelope through the ordinary completion path, and advances ONLY
  after that checkpoint succeeds. The emitting port is now BOUND into each signal connection --
  Godot signals do not tell a handler who emitted, so accepts completion only from the configured
 port identity was previously unenforceable rather than merely unenforced.
* LATENT BUG FOUND AND FIXED. SUBSTAGE_CONTRACTS was declared in Task 7 and NEVER CONSULTED:
  _commit_completion validated every record against STAGE_CONTRACTS[stage_id], so any substage
  driven through the coordinator would have been rejected for a kind mismatch
  (schedule_entry_complete vs schedule_actions_complete). No test reached it -- the entry-substage
  suites drive the state port and lifecycle directly, and the only coordinator-driven walk commits
  an empty Schedule, which has no substages. Wiring the date presentation is what finally routes a
  substage through there. Now validated by receipt KIND through its own contract.
* BOOTSTRAP. The same two retained objects the start port was built from are injected into the
  state port. get_desktop_contract_state() gains presentation_producer_ready, deliberately false,
  asserted false, exactly as dating_presentation_ready is.

NEW TESTS

* tests/integration/test_committed_schedule_presentation_resume.gd (8 tests) -- Step 8.2. A crash
  DESTROYS and rebuilds every process owner from the same on-disk root plus the persisted lifecycle
  bytes. Proven: the restored resolution derives the byte-identical intent and completion children;
  ordinals never renumber across a crash at the first of two surviving dates; a restored port
  re-issues the identical command and the fresh owner derives the SAME token; a duplicate physical
  end publishes nothing further; a restored owner replaying a settled record causes no second
  publication; an invented token returns physical_completion_untrusted; a checkpointed presentation
  is never offered again; a Hospital-superseded date presents nothing and carries no presentation
  evidence.
* tests/support/FakeDesktopConsequenceSource.gd -- schema-exact Plan-02 fixture. Every receipt id
  is minted through a REAL issuer, so the ancestry Plan 01 binds is genuinely anchored rather than
  a nonblank String. Full 10-member board-fate shape with both source_action fields exactly null,
  per plan line 532. NEVER a bootstrap dependency.
* 3 tests in test_day_resolution_plan.gd for the persisted root and its re-proof on load.
* 1 test in test_desktop_bootstrap_wiring.gd asserting the producer gap.

RE-BASELINED (the fail-closed law made these RED for the right reason)

tests/integration/test_committed_schedule_effect_order.gd -- its four Hospital-triggered tests now
configure the producer and carry the resolution through a REAL Hospital presentation: the real
DialogicPresentationOwnerAdapter over a real DialogicBridge, completing on
_on_runtime_timeline_ended. Nothing fabricates evidence that a presentation happened. The suite is
strictly stronger than before.

WHAT IT PROVES, and why it is not a duplicate of the port suites

The port suites prove the PORT validates what it is handed. The resume suite
proves the producer is DETERMINISTIC across a crash. Neither proves the producer
emits the bytes the MATRIX specifies. A producer that omitted source_day from its
projection, or sorted input_receipt_ids differently, would have passed both and
then forked the identity chain the moment any other consumer derived the same row.

METHOD. Every expectation is rebuilt from plan lines 97, 98 and 100 read as TEXT,
not from the producer's code path. The suite constructs the exact P(path,value)
token set the matrix names, asks the SAME issuer to derive a child from it, and
requires the resulting child id to equal the one the producer actually emitted.
derive_child is a deterministic function of (parent, kind, ordinal, sorted
sources), so equal ids mean the two projections agreed member for member. A
missing, extra, renamed, reordered or differently serialised member cannot
survive that comparison.

THE SWEEP HAS TEETH -- VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. Each of the intent's 13 members and
the completion's 7 is perturbed alone and required to move the child id. To
confirm the sweep is not vacuous I removed P(stage_index,...) from the
producer's projection and re-ran: 5 tests failed, reporting the two differing
child ids. The implementation was then restored and re-verified.

ALSO COVERED
* parent and ordinal are load-bearing (a foreign root and ordinal 1 both differ)
* member ORDER is NOT load-bearing, because S(...) sorts -- two honest producers
  of the same row cannot disagree purely on iteration order -- while dropping a
  member does change the id
* the completion names its intent in substage_id and never names itself, so it is
  structurally underivable before its prerequisite exists (plan line 100)
* line 100's L([condition_receipt_id] + hospital_miss_receipt_ids) still contains
  the condition id when Hospital supersedes NO date, i.e. the concatenation is
  flattened rather than emptied
* the Hospital variant carries the four-member Hospital context and the Dating
  variant the four-member Dating context; neither borrows the other's shape
* an underivable presentation refuses with the substage still PENDING, so the
  refusal genuinely precedes any physical start or stage mutation

ROBUSTNESS GAP FOUND BY THE SUITE AND FIXED

A plan can carry a valid resolution root while the PORT handling it has no
configured issuer -- a half-composed process, or a resolution begun by one port
and resumed by another. That path dereferenced a null issuer part-way through
derivation (Cannot call method 'call' on a null value) instead of failing
closed. It now returns presentation_intent_unavailable with the stage still
pending. This was a real defect, not a test artefact.

EVIDENCE
Wide regression: exit 0 | 38 scripts | 509 tests | 509 passing | 6460 asserts
log .godot/phase2r_logs/p2r18-regression.log
Matrix suite alone: exit 0 | 12 tests | 816 asserts
log .godot/phase2r_logs/p2r18-matrix.log
Mutation probe (stage_index removed, expected RED): 5 failing
log .godot/phase2r_logs/p2r18-mutation-probe.log

STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD

* SceneRouter.route_presentation() has no caller in the walk. The coordinator
  returns the await_registered_command result carrying route_id and the
  presentation_request; who dispatches it is a live-desktop concern and Plan 03
  owns the Done dispatch surface.
* The producer is unreachable in production until Plan 02 configures the
  desktop-consequence source (DEVIATION-5). Asserted false by the bootstrap probe.
* The deferred-pair variant is implemented and reachable but is not yet exercised
  end to end by a test; the Hospital and surviving-date variants are.

dwm-p2r.18 IS NOT CLOSED. dwm-p2r.14 IS NOT CLOSED. No push was made. A fresh
review pass over the whole .14/.18 boundary is recommended before either closes
and .15 is claimed.

comments.author: Siuuuers
comments.text:
COLD REVIEW of db7c290b..8fd45c4c (four commits, codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed). Done in
two passes: the whole audit against the plan matrix FIRST, the author's review brief
only afterwards. No subagents. Nothing committed, nothing pushed, no bead closed.

GATES RE-RUN VERBATIM AT 8fd45c4c -- both reproduce the recorded figures exactly

  Step 8.8 presentation_day7_green: exit 0 | 12 scripts | 162 tests | 162 passing |
    1916 asserts | 0 SUITE_NOT_EXECUTED
  Step 7.7 hospital_order_green:    exit 0 | 11 scripts | 135 tests | 135 passing |
    1868 asserts | 0 SUITE_NOT_EXECUTED

Orphans 24 in both, i.e. the known GUT-owned constant. Neither gate includes
test_committed_schedule_presentation_matrix.gd, so both remain green after the test
work below.

=================================================================================
FINDING 1 (NEW, NOT IN THE BRIEF, HIGHEST SEVERITY)
THE DEFERRED-PAIR VARIANT CANNOT FIRE. IT IS UNREACHABLE, NOT MERELY UNTESTED.
=================================================================================

The brief records the pair as "implemented and reachable but not exercised end to
end". It is implemented and NOT reachable.

_deferred_pair_site() (GameStateDayResolutionPort.gd:851-853) reads
contacts.group_action.deferred_twofriends. That key does not exist and CANNOT exist:
group_action is validated against _GROUP_ACTION_KEYS, a 9-member exact set enforced
by _has_exact_keys with a size() equality check (ContactInvitationState.gd:49-52,
:1035). deferred_twofriends is a member of the resolve_day_end RECEIPT
(ContactInvitationState.gd:482, :509), never of group_action. So .get() returns null,
the TYPE_DICTIONARY check fails, and the site returns {} on every call.

PROVEN ON THE REAL SUBSTRATE, not by reading. The new test drives the canonical pair
to ACCEPTED through the real Contacts owner, calls the real
resolve_invitations_for_day with group_outcome=not_attended, confirms the returned
receipt carries deferred_twofriends.action_id == "group:priscilla_lavinia:day2" --
the deferral genuinely happened -- and then fails at the read location:

  [Failed]: [0] expected to equal [27]: the deferral must be readable where the
  producer reads it, or the variant never fires

(0 = TYPE_NIL, 27 = TYPE_DICTIONARY.) The end-to-end test fails with:

  [Failed]: the twofriends_if_deferred stage completed with
  mode=complete_immediately and no presentation, so the producer derived no
  presentation intent for it

TWO FURTHER LAYERS, so a one-line read fix is likely not sufficient:

  (a) ENTRY LOOKUP SCOPE. Even with the read corrected, _deferred_pair_site searches
      _active_committed_entries() -- THIS resolution's frozen aggregate. A deferral by
      definition names a pair missed on an EARLIER day, so its committed entry belongs
      to a prior aggregate and will not be found here.
  (b) VARIANT OVERLAP. If the group entry IS in the current aggregate it is not
      deferred yet, and ACTION_KIND_STAGES routes action_kind="group" to
      execute_schedule_dates. So it presents as the "group" surviving-date variant at
      stage 5 before twofriends_if_deferred at stage 6 is ever reached. Nothing makes
      the two variants mutually exclusive; line 100 lists them as distinct rows.

=================================================================================
FINDING 2: MATRIX DIVERGENCE THE MATRIX SUITE STRUCTURALLY CANNOT CATCH
=================================================================================

_presentation_command projects _project("stage_id", str(stage["transaction_id"])).
For a surviving date, `stage` is the SUBSTAGE cursor record (DayResolutionPlan.gd
_substage_record, :626-631), whose transaction_id is
resolution_id + ":surviving_date:<n>:<entry_id>".

Plan line 100 requires: "stage_id is the exact TOP-LEVEL P01.day_resolution.stage
child ID and substage_id is the exact persisted P01.presentation.intent child ID."
Under DEVIATION-4's synthetic scheme the top-level id is
resolution_id + ":execute_schedule_dates". Line 100 explicitly distinguishes
top-level rows (role="day_resolution.stage") from entry-substage rows
(role="day_resolution.entry_substage"), so "top-level" is not satisfied by a
substage id. Hospital and the deferred pair are top-level stages and so are correct
by accident of shape; only the surviving-date variant diverges.

WHY THE SUITE MISSES IT. _expected_completion_projection()
(test_committed_schedule_presentation_matrix.gd:370-377) reads stage_id, substage_id,
route_id, timeline_id and context_sha256 back out of the producer's OWN request. Only
`role` is independently rebuilt from the plan text. So the completion row's
conformance test is circular on every member that could diverge, and the
load-bearing sweep cannot help: perturbing a member that was sourced from the
producer still moves the id.

This qualifies the brief's claim that the suite rebuilds "the 13 intent members and 7
completion members" from the text. It holds for the intent -- stage_name, stage_index,
route_id, presentation_kind, schedule_entry_id and input_receipt_ids are genuinely
independent there. It does not hold for the completion.

=================================================================================
FINDING 3: _validate_resolution_root RE-PROOF GAPS
=================================================================================

  (a) NO ANCESTRY EDGE. It checks start["receipt_provenance"] is a Dictionary but
      never that it descends from root["receipt_id"]. A tampered snapshot can pair a
      genuine root R with a start receipt derived under a DIFFERENT root, provided the
      start receipt's resolution_id string matches. The producer then derives every
      presentation child under R while projecting day_resolution_start_receipt_id from
      the foreign receipt. The docstring's "must carry full provenance rather than an
      id" is literally true; the edge it implies is unchecked.
  (b) causal_day_instance IS NOT REQUIRED but IS INDEXED RAW. _presentation_command
      does str(start_receipt["causal_day_instance"]) and _derive_hospital_rows does
      str(start["causal_day_instance"]). A restored plan that passes
      _validate_resolution_root with that key absent CRASHES the walk instead of
      failing closed. source_day and resolution_id are both validated; this one is not.

=================================================================================
FINDING 4: HOSPITAL `required` IS READ LIVE TWICE, BRACKETING THE PRESENTATION
=================================================================================

_hospital_site() gates on _game_state.should_route_hospital() at stage-begin.
_hospital_envelope() re-reads the SAME live flag at stage-completion (reached via
presentation_stage_receipt -> _immediate_receipt) and re-runs
HOSPITAL_RULES.plan_resolution. If anything between the two reads clears the flag,
the intent claims required=true while the checkpointed stage receipt records
required=false with superseded_entry_ids=[], silently un-superseding every date AFTER
the Hospital presentation played. Nothing compares the completion-time read to the
derivation-time read. This is the same class as the superseded=false literal the brief
flags, but with a live re-read rather than a constant, and the file elsewhere enforces
the opposite rule ("never from live state" on _committed_entry).

=================================================================================
SMALLER ITEMS
=================================================================================

  * _stage_index() returns Array.find() = -1 unchecked, while _presentation_ordinal
    immediately beside it IS checked for < 0 and fails closed. Unreachable today: the
    D7 stage array contains none of the three presentation stages.
  * _presentation_context hardcodes PAIR_PARTICIPANTS for kind=="group", ignoring the
    committed entry's own participants, and _presentation_timeline_id builds the group
    locator from PAIR_SLUG. Two group dates with different participants would produce
    the same context_sha256 and the same timeline. Correct only if "group == the P-L
    pair" is a domain invariant; nothing here reads or asserts it. Same literal-vs-read
    shape the brief already flags for superseded=false.
  * complete_presentation_stage() returns early on code==duplicate_transaction WITHOUT
    clearing _awaiting or _last_presentation_completion and without calling resume(),
    leaving the coordinator permanently "awaiting" a stage the plan already completed.
    Asymmetric with the success path; no test covers it.
  * hospital_miss_receipt_ids are RE-DERIVED on every _presentation_command call and
    never written into the plan; line 100 says "the exact array of PERSISTED
    P01.hospital.miss child IDs". Determinism covers it and the resume suite proves
    byte-identity, but the deviation is not recorded alongside DEVIATION-4/5.
  * "the receipt is inside the bytes the checkpoint DURABLY records" overstates:
    _disk_write_for returns {kind: none} for every resolution stage, so this is an
    in-memory checkpoint-port commit, not a disk write. Pre-existing architecture, not
    a regression -- only the wording is stronger than the mechanism.

=================================================================================
CONFIRMED CORRECT (audited, no defect found)
=================================================================================

  * IDEMPOTENCE AGREEMENT. str(resolution_start.get("command_id", resolution_id)) is
    the IDENTICAL expression in RunLifecycle.begin_day_resolution,
    RunLifecycle.prepare_day_resolution AND DayResolutionPlan.create, so the fallback
    cannot drift between them. _resolution_start short-circuits on a matching persisted
    command_id BEFORE touching the issuer, so a replayed Done command does not mint and
    discard a root. The unconfigured path sets resolution_id == command_id, so a plan
    created before the producer was configured still matches a later configured replay.
    I could not construct a disagreement.
  * CHECKPOINT-THEN-ADVANCE. Genuinely correct: prepare_completion -> checkpoint.prepare
    -> checkpoint.commit -> state.commit -> publish, with checkpoint rolled back alone
    on checkpoint failure and BOTH rolled back on state_commit/publish failure. The
    stage advances only after the checkpoint commits.
  * THE BRIEF'S 4th WEAK POINT IS REFUTED AS A WORRY. The path where a plan exists, is
    complete, and carries a different command_id is CORRECT by design: it mints a new
    root and replaces the completed plan, which is what a new day's Done command should
    do. The port's _plan_is_complete is byte-identical to DayResolutionPlan.is_complete
    (both check only top-level stage state), so the two cannot disagree.
  * _validate_substage_envelope covers every kind a substage can actually return
    (schedule_entry_complete for ordinary_action, schedule_date_complete for
    surviving_date). The SUBSTAGE_CONTRACTS dead-table fix is real.

=================================================================================
WORKING TREE (uncommitted; HEAD still 8fd45c4c)
=================================================================================

M tests/integration/test_committed_schedule_presentation_matrix.gd  (+222)

Two RED tests added, per user decision, as the executable record of Finding 1:

  test_the_deferred_pair_marker_is_visible_where_the_producer_reads_it
  test_the_deferred_pair_variant_carries_its_exact_matrix_row

The second asserts the full line-97 row for the pair -- ordinal 0, the Dating context
shape, L(schedule_entry_id, source_receipt_id), stage_index 6, and the load-bearing
sweep over all 13 members -- so it becomes real coverage the moment the producer is
fixed, rather than needing to be rewritten. The marker is produced by the REAL owner
(resolve_invitations_for_day); nothing is written into contacts by hand, deliberately,
because hand-writing the marker would have made the test pass against a state shape
production can never produce, cementing the bug.

Suite now: exit 1 | 14 tests | 12 passing | 2 failing | 865/867 asserts. Each new test
fails EXACTLY ONCE with a message naming the cause.

Step 8.8 and Step 7.7 both stay green -- neither includes this suite. The wide
regression does (the author's own 497 -> 509 jump across 37 -> 38 scripts is exactly
this suite's 12 tests), so by arithmetic it becomes 511 tests / 509 passing / 2 failing
/ exit 1. I did NOT re-run it: its exact suite list is not recorded anywhere readable
from this worktree, and inventing a list would produce a number that is not the gate.

comments.text:
CORRECTION TO THE PRECEDING REVIEW COMMENT, AND THE FIX FOR FINDING 1.

FINDING 1 WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE DEFECT AND WRONG ABOUT ITS DEPTH.

The core defect stands and is confirmed: _deferred_pair_site read
contacts.group_action.deferred_twofriends, a key that cannot exist because
group_action is validated against an exact 9-member record shape
(_GROUP_ACTION_KEYS + _has_exact_keys size check). The site returned {} on every
call and the twofriends_if_deferred variant never fired.

But the two "further layers" I listed as making this a design question are BOTH
answered by the plan, and I should have checked before calling it one.

Plan line 1057: Hospital "marks every committed date prevented_by_fainting exactly
once before any dating board, records distinct hospital miss receipts, completes
recovery, THEN permits deferred pair presentation, invitation rollover, and day
advance."

So the deferred pair is a SAME-RESOLUTION consequence of Hospital, not a
cross-day carry-over. That resolves both layers:

  (a) ENTRY LOOKUP SCOPE -- not a problem. The pair's committed entry IS in this
      resolution's frozen aggregate, because Hospital superseded it today.
      HOSPITAL_RULES.DATE_KINDS is ["solo","group"], so a committed group entry is
      superseded and gets its own P01.hospital.miss like any date.
  (b) VARIANT OVERLAP -- not a problem, and in fact the opposite. Because the entry
      is superseded, _surviving_date_site already refuses it at execute_schedule_dates.
      The two variants are mutually exclusive by construction, exactly as that
      function's existing comment claims.

The remaining question was only WHERE the pair stage learns it is owed a
presentation, and the answer was already in the file: _superseded_entry_ids(),
which reads the supersession the Hospital transaction DURABLY committed, out of its
stage receipt rather than from live state.

THE FIX (uncommitted; see WORKING TREE below)

  * _deferred_pair_entry_id() -- new; returns the committed group entry this
    resolution's Hospital superseded, or "". Reads _superseded_entry_ids() plus the
    frozen aggregate. No live invitation field is consulted at all.
  * _deferred_pair_site() -- now a thin wrapper over it, symmetric with
    _surviving_date_site.
  * _immediate_receipt("twofriends_if_deferred") -- `required` was a hardcoded
    false; it is now the same fact _deferred_pair_site presents on. A stage that
    presented the pair and then checkpointed required=false would have recorded a
    receipt contradicting its own presentation. No existing test asserted the old
    literal; the fixtures that mention twofriends_resolution are separate fakes.

THE TESTS WERE REWRITTEN TO THE PLAN'S SCENARIO

My first draft set the deferral up through resolve_invitations_for_day with
group_outcome=not_attended and no Hospital. That is the WRONG scenario for Plan 01:
that path's deferral is produced at invitation_rollover, a LATER stage than
twofriends_if_deferred, so it cannot be what this stage reads, and on the next day
the entry is no longer in the aggregate. Landing that test would have asserted
something the plan does not require. Both tests now drive a real Hospital
supersession instead:

  test_hospital_supersession_is_what_owes_the_pair_a_presentation
    -- asserts the durable Hospital receipt superseded exactly the committed pair
       entry, and that the presentation is for exactly that entry.
  test_the_deferred_pair_variant_carries_its_exact_matrix_row
    -- ordinal 0, presentation_kind/stage_name/route_id/schedule_entry_id per line
       100, the Dating context shape (and NOT the Hospital one), timeline
       dating.twofriends.priscilla_lavinia.day2.pre_challenge, stage_index 6,
       input_receipt_ids = L(schedule_entry_id, source_receipt_id), the full line-97
       row rebuilt from plan text and derived through the same issuer, plus the
       load-bearing sweep over all 13 members.

The group pair is seeded through the REAL Contacts owner (offer both solos ->
activate_group_after_round -> open -> reply), so the acceptance receipt the
committed entry resolves to is genuinely anchored.

EVIDENCE AT THE CURRENT (UNCOMMITTED) TREE -- all exit 0, no SUITE_NOT_EXECUTED

  Step 8.8 presentation_day7_green: 12 scripts | 162 tests | 162 passing | 1916 asserts
  Step 7.7 hospital_order_green:    11 scripts | 135 tests | 135 passing | 1868 asserts
  matrix suite alone:                1 script  |  14 tests |  14 passing | 1085 asserts
  affected-suite regression:        10 scripts | 125 tests | 125 passing | 2311 asserts
    (presentation_resume, presentation_matrix, committed_schedule_day_resolution,
     run_lifecycle, run_lifecycle_plan_seams, run_plan_succession,
     day_resolution_snapshot_production, day_resolution_start_port, save_migrations,
     run_snapshot_schema)

Both named gates are byte-for-byte the same counts as before the fix, so nothing
regressed; the matrix suite went 12/14 RED -> 14/14 green.

FINDINGS 2, 3 AND 4 OF THE PRECEDING COMMENT ARE UNTOUCHED AND STILL OPEN

  2. completion stage_id names the SUBSTAGE, not the top-level stage, for the
     surviving-date variant (plan line 100), and _expected_completion_projection
     cannot catch it because it reads that member back out of the producer.
  3. _validate_resolution_root proves no ancestry edge from start receipt to root,
     and does not require causal_day_instance that the producer then indexes raw.
  4. Hospital `required` is read live twice, bracketing the physical presentation,
     with no cross-check.

Plus the smaller items: unchecked _stage_index -1, hardcoded PAIR_PARTICIPANTS for
kind=="group", complete_presentation_stage not clearing _awaiting on
duplicate_transaction, and hospital_miss_receipt_ids re-derived rather than persisted.

TWO OPERATIONAL NOTES WORTH KEEPING, both cost a failed attempt here.

1. Invoke-ExactPathCommit.ps1 passes the message as `git commit -m $Message`.
   Windows PowerShell 5.1 mangles a native-command argument that contains
   embedded DOUBLE QUOTES, so a message quoting plan text verbatim makes git exit
   nonzero and the script reports only its own `git commit failed.` with git's
   stderr swallowed by Invoke-GitSafe. Keep commit messages free of double quotes
   and backticks, or teach the script to use `-F <file>` instead. The beads
   pre-commit and prepare-commit-msg hooks were both verified green and were NOT
   the cause.
2. When the script throws at the commit step it leaves the index STAGED, and its
   own entry guard then refuses the retry with `Staged index is not empty.`
   Unstage with `git restore --staged <paths>` before re-running. The working
   tree is untouched by this.

commit changed no file contents, only their tracked state)

  3. _validate_resolution_root proves no ancestry edge from the start receipt to

BOTH HALVES CONFIRMED IN THE SOURCE BEFORE FIXING, not taken from the review.

(a) NO ANCESTRY EDGE. _validate_resolution_root checked only
typeof(start.get("receipt_provenance")) == TYPE_DICTIONARY. Full provenance sitting BESIDE a
root proves nothing until it is tied to THAT root, so a tampered snapshot could pair a genuine
root R with a start receipt derived under a DIFFERENT root as long as the start receipt's
resolution_id string still matched. The producer would then anchor every presentation child
under R while projecting day_resolution_start_receipt_id from the foreign receipt. That forged
chain reproduces byte-identically on every later load, which is what makes it invisible
downstream.

The edge is exactly the issuer's own provenance record (DesktopIdentityNonceIssuer.derive_child
builds {schema_version, parent_receipt_id, child_kind, ordinal, source_ids, child_id}), so two
checks close it:
  provenance.parent_receipt_id == root.receipt_id   -- derived under THIS root
  provenance.child_id          == start.receipt_id  -- and IS the child it claims to be
The second is the same class and one line: the intent projects str(start["receipt_id"]), so a
swapped receipt_id under honest provenance forks the chain just as effectively.

(b) causal_day_instance REQUIRED, NOT COERCED. Repo grep for raw indexes into the start receipt
returns exactly two members: receipt_id (already validated nonempty) and causal_day_instance,
read raw at GameStateDayResolutionPort.gd:966, :1089, :1116 and :1135. It was never required
here, so a restored plan missing it passed validation and CRASHED the walk instead of failing
closed at the boundary. Now required as a nonblank String; a non-String is refused rather than
coerced, because str() would change the projected bytes without changing the shape.
