comments.text:
FINDING 4 CLOSED. Commit 0dea588ee717f58586b8be9116184e69e5a16460, parent
26b9f932ad0d0a29964dc6b0e2af88759dbc7fdc, branch codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed. Landed through
tools/git/Invoke-ExactPathCommit.ps1 with an exact 2-path RequiredStatus map:
EXACT_PATH_COMMIT: PASS. AllowedDirtyPaths: evidence/phase_2r/logs/isolated-godot.jsonl.
No push. ALL FOUR REVIEW FINDINGS ARE NOW CLOSED -- but see NEW FINDING 5 below before
claiming dwm-p2r.15.

THE DEFECT, REPRODUCED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED

_hospital_site() reads _game_state.should_route_hospital() at stage-BEGIN to decide whether to
derive a presentation. _hospital_envelope() read the same live flag again at stage-COMPLETION,
so the physical presentation sat between two independent reads of a mutable value with nothing
comparing them. The new test clears the flag in exactly that window and, against the old code,
the checkpointed receipt recorded:

  required=false, superseded_entry_ids=[]   (date_schedule_entry_ids still listed the date)

i.e. the Hospital presentation played, and then the stage silently un-superseded the very date
it had just been played for. Exactly the failure the review predicted.

THE FIX, AND WHY IT NEEDS NO NEW PERSISTED SLOT

I expected this to need the derivation-time answer stored somewhere and was ready to argue
about where. It does not, because the answer is already implied by durable facts:

• A Hospital presentation EXISTS only because _hospital_site() said required.
• DayResolutionCoordinator.complete_presentation_stage refuses a completion whose receipt_id is
  not the awaiting request's completion_transaction_id, so reaching presentation_stage_receipt
  proves a lawful Hospital presentation settled.
• Every OTHER input to the envelope already comes from the frozen aggregate
  (_active_committed_entries) rather than live state, so `required` was the last live read in it.

So the completion path carries presented=true and the envelope uses it instead of re-reading.
_immediate_receipt gained an optional `presented` flag threaded only into _hospital_envelope;
the twofriends branch is untouched (its `required` already reads the durable supersession), and
the immediate path is unchanged -- there, begin and completion happen inside one
begin_next_stage() call with no presentation between them, so the two reads cannot diverge.

Rejected alternatives, recorded so they are not re-litigated:
• Fail closed on disagreement instead of carrying the answer. Refused: the timeline has already
  physically played by then, so refusing strands the run at a stage whose effect happened.
• Make the Plan-02 condition receipt the authority (it carries decision/danger). Refused: the
  consequence source is deliberately unconfigured in production (DEVIATION-5), so every ordinary
  no-Hospital day would start failing closed. That binding is Plan 02's call, not Plan 01's.
• Persist `required` into the stage record or PLAN_KEYS. Not needed for this defect, and it is
  the DEVIATION-4-shaped ripple through RunSnapshotSchema / SaveDocument v3 / migrations.

NEW FINDING 5, FOUND WHILE FIXING 4 -- NOT FIXED, AND IT BLOCKS .15

The same live flag has a SECOND window, and this one is a crash window rather than a
presentation window. On resume, DayResolutionCoordinator.resume() calls the port's
begin_next_stage() again for the still-ACTIVE Hospital stage, which re-runs _presentation_site()
-- another live read of should_route_hospital(). DayResolutionPlan.begin_stage is idempotent on
an already-active stage, so nothing objects.

Consequence: if the flag is clear when the process comes back (a restore that rebuilt GameState
from a save written before the faint, or any owner that resets it), the resumed walk derives NO
presentation for a stage that already published a P01.presentation.intent, and completes it with
required=false. The intent is orphaned and the resolution's children are not the ones it
already committed to -- the same class of corruption dwm-p2r.18 exists to prevent, one layer up.

Today's fix does not reach this: it makes the COMPLETION agree with the derivation, but the
re-derivation itself is still live-sourced. Closing it genuinely does require the derivation-time
answer to be durable, which is the PLAN_KEYS/stage-record change above, or Plan 02's condition
receipt becoming the authority. Both are bigger than this bead and one is Plan 02's to make.

WHY THE RESUME SUITE DOES NOT CATCH IT: test_committed_schedule_presentation_resume.gd leaves
pending_hospital set across every Step 8.2 cut, so the live re-read always returns the same
answer. The gap is real but unexercised.

gate members; no pre-existing test changed.

Before the fix the effect_order suite was 9 tests | 8 passing | 1 failing | 319/322 asserts.

STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD

Plus the smaller items, all still untouched: unchecked _stage_index -1, hardcoded
PAIR_PARTICIPANTS for kind=="group", complete_presentation_stage not clearing _awaiting on

scope call for the human, not for the implementer.

comments.text:
SMALLER ITEMS SWEPT. Commit ed29271f1c0b5fd733dca002399147e78416cc09, parent
0dea588ee717f58586b8be9116184e69e5a16460, branch codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed.

AllowedDirtyPaths: evidence/phase_2r/logs/isolated-godot.jsonl. No push.

Finding 5 was also filed as its own bead rather than fixed here -- see dwm-p2r.19 below.

THE BIGGEST THING FOUND WAS NOT ON THE LIST

complete_presentation_stage() had ZERO callers anywhere in the repo. Not in production, where
Plan 03 still owns the Done dispatch, and not in a single test. The suites that drive real
presentations (effect_order, presentation_resume, presentation_matrix) call the state port's
presentation_stage_receipt() and then complete the stage through RunLifecycle directly, which
bypasses the coordinator's ordering entirely. So "the coordinator checkpoints the port's
completion receipt before advancing the stage" -- a dwm-p2r.14 acceptance criterion, and the
review's own CONFIRMED CORRECT entry -- was true by reading and unproven by execution.

Three tests now reach it, through a new minimal fake
(tests/support/FakePresentationPort.gd, 4 members plus two signals):

  test_a_published_completion_is_checkpointed_and_then_advances_the_stage
    -- and asserts the SIGNAL ALONE checkpoints nothing and advances nothing
  test_a_completion_that_does_not_settle_the_awaiting_command_is_refused
    -- stage left ACTIVE, code presentation_completion_untrusted
  test_a_duplicate_completion_does_not_leave_the_coordinator_awaiting_a_finished_stage

The first two PASS against the pre-fix code. That is the point: they characterise behaviour that
was already correct, and they are what makes the third test's failure meaningful rather than a
symptom of a degenerate harness. FakeDayResolutionStatePort gained
set_registered_presentation(), because without a presentation_request the awaiting command
carries no completion_transaction_id and the coordinator's "does this receipt settle THIS
command" check would have passed vacuously on two empty strings.

ITEM 1 -- DUPLICATE COMPLETION (fixed). complete_presentation_stage returned on
duplicate_transaction BEFORE dropping _awaiting and _last_presentation_completion, so a plan that
had already completed the stage left the coordinator awaiting a finished one: every later call
returned duplicate again and this path never reached resume(). Both are now dropped exactly as on
the success path, while the duplicate is still REPORTED rather than resumed over, since nothing
new was checkpointed.

Deliberately NOT applied to complete_route_stage, which has the same early return. There the
transaction id comes from _registered_history and may be an OLDER transaction whose replay must
leave a newer awaiting command alone; here it is read from _awaiting itself, so it cannot be.
Same shape, different correctness argument. Flagging rather than changing it.

ITEM 2 -- UNCHECKED _stage_index -1 (fixed). Guarded like the ordinal beside it, returning
invalid_presentation_stage_index. Array.find() returns -1 for a stage the day's frozen array does
not carry, and -1 is a perfectly projectable int: it would anchor a child under a stage_index
naming no stage rather than refusing. Unreachable today, which is exactly why it is guarded now
rather than left for a future day's stage array to discover.

ITEM 3 -- HARDCODED PAIR_PARTICIPANTS (no code change; the review's worry does not hold).
Checked rather than assumed: ScheduleActionRegistry REFUSES any group action whose participants
are not exactly ["priscilla","lavinia"] in that order ("a reversed pair is a tamper, not a
synonym"), and ContactInvitationState mints every group action_id as group:priscilla_lavinia:dayN
against an exact-match check. A committed group entry is validated against that registry under
the fingerprint it was committed with. So two group dates with different participants cannot both
exist to collide on one context hash: the hardcode is correct. What was missing was any pointer
from here to where the invariant is enforced, so that is now recorded at the constant. Left as a
literal deliberately -- reading participants off the entry would be strictly weaker, since the
entry's array is draft-supplied while the registry record's is law.

ITEM 4 -- hospital_miss_receipt_ids RE-DERIVED (recorded, not changed). Now DEVIATION-6 in
docs/superpowers/notes/2026-08-18-p2r18-review-brief.md, alongside 4 and 5, which is what the
review actually asked for. Determinism covers the deviation and the resume suite proves
byte-identity; persisting the array is a PLAN_KEYS change with the DEVIATION-4 ripple and nothing
needs it yet.

FINDING 5 FILED AS dwm-p2r.19 (P1, bug, parent dwm-p2r, blocks dwm-p2r.15)
"Anchor Hospital condition truth so a resumed walk re-derives the same presentation"

It carries both options costed out and picks NEITHER, because the choice is a human scope call:
OPTION A persists the derived answer in Plan 01 (PLAN_KEYS/STAGE_KEYS are exact sets, so it
ripples into RunSnapshotSchema, SaveDocument v3, migrations and fixtures -- the DEVIATION-4 blast
radius, with precedent from this very bead); OPTION B makes the Plan-02 condition receipt the
authority (arguably where condition truth belonged all along, but the consequence source is
deliberately unconfigured in production, so every ordinary no-Hospital day would start failing
closed until Plan 02 lands -- making it a Plan 02 sequencing decision). The bead also records
that only the Hospital variant has this problem, and a DO NOT against fixing it with an
in-memory answer.

production callers of SceneRouter.route_presentation() AND zero production callers of the

P01.presentation.intent, the walk paused carrying its route_id and presentation_request, and the

TWO SCOPE DECISIONS, BOTH TAKEN BY THE MAINTAINER RATHER THAN ASSUMED

1. WHERE THE DISPATCH LIVES: inside DayResolutionCoordinator.resume(). The coordinator is the object
that PAUSES the walk on a presentation, so it is the object that must be able to launch one. The
rejected alternative was a separate dispatch_presentation() the caller invokes afterwards, which
would have left the adapters are actually launched resting on a production caller that does not
exist -- the same gap this bead exists to close.
2. WHAT A FAILED LAUNCH DOES: fail closed, stage ACTIVE and unreceipted. Nothing is rolled back and
nothing needs to be -- no receipt, no domain mutation, and _awaiting keeps this exact command. The
rejected alternative was to skip dispatch silently when no router is configured, which would let a
mis-composed graph reach a presentation stage and show nothing.

THE ORDER IS FORCED, NOT CHOSEN. route_presentation hands the off-tree scene the CANONICAL command --
the request plus command_sha256 and the owner-derived physical_token -- and only begin() produces
those bytes, so the physical presentation necessarily starts before the scene opens. That makes the
order of the CHECKS load-bearing: route id, then router, then port are all validated before begin()
runs, so a route that cannot be shown is refused before a timeline starts behind it. No redundant
is_ready() pre-check was added: is_ready() is false exactly when the port has no physical owner, and

begin() with dating_physical_owner_unconfigured and never reaches the router.

FOUND BY COLD REVIEW OF db6f379c1, not by a failing gate. The launch that db6f379c1 added is
dispatched from resume(), and resume() had no re-entry guard: it re-derived the awaiting command,
overwrote _awaiting, and launched again unconditionally. Proved by probe before any fix, against
unmodified production:

  SECOND RESUME code=await_registered_command routes=2 begins=2

WHY THE PHYSICAL LAYER WAS ALREADY SAFE AND THE SCENE LAYER WAS NOT. HospitalPresentationPort.begin
caches per completion_transaction_id and DialogicPresentationOwnerAdapter.begin_physical refuses to
restart an in-flight timeline, so no timeline replays -- that half was already double-guarded and
this change does not touch it. SceneRouter.route_presentation carries no such guard: it instantiates
the PackedScene, reassigns tree.current_scene, and queue_frees the previous one. So a second resume()
while a presentation was showing tore down the live scene and rebuilt it underneath a timeline that
kept playing, taking every signal connection the freed scene held with it.

REACHABILITY. Latent, not live. GameState.resume_day_resolution() and begin_day_resolution_stage()
have zero production callers today, consistent with DEVIATION-5 -- but they are exactly the seams
Plan 03 will drive, and the only retry coverage db6f379c1 shipped was failure-then-resume, where
re-dispatch is the DESIRED behaviour. Success-then-resume was untested and behaved differently.

WHAT LANDED. DayResolutionCoordinator gains _launched_transaction. _launch_presentation returns {}
when the awaiting transaction is already showing, and records the transaction ONLY after a route
that actually opened. The field is cleared in lockstep with _awaiting at both existing clear sites.
resume() itself is UNCHANGED -- the guard lives inside the function that owns the dispatch, so the
call site added by db6f379c1 is untouched. The field is deliberately NOT persisted: after a crash
the port cache and the owner in-flight map are empty too, so a fresh process SHOULD re-launch.

PROVEN RED FIRST, then by mutation.

1. The test was written and run against unmodified production BEFORE the guard existed: 21/22,
   EXACTLY ONE test red, on exactly the two assertions naming the defect -- routes 2 expected 1 and
   begins 2 expected 1. Every other test in the suite stayed green. Then 22/22 with the guard.
2. MUTATION: record the launch even when the route was refused. 21/22, EXACTLY ONE test red, and it
   is the PRE-EXISTING test_a_refused_route_leaves_the_stage_active_and_replays_the_identical_command

the guard alone):

- THE CHECK-ORDER CLAIM IS AN OVERCLAIM. The note and the _launch_presentation docstring both say
  route id, then router, then port are all validated before begin() runs, so a route that cannot be
  shown is refused before a timeline starts behind it. What is actually validated before begin() is
  that a route surface object and a port object EXIST. Whether the scene can be SHOWN is decided
  inside route_presentation, after begin() has reached bridge.start_timeline_id: ports unconfigured
  (SceneRouter.gd:113), scene missing (:129), scene unconfigurable (:135), configure_presentation
  refused (:139), tree unavailable (:144). The committed suite contains its own counter-example --
  test_a_refused_route_leaves_the_stage_active_and_replays_the_identical_command arms the router with

  begun. Mutation 2 in the previous comment proved the router-NULL ordering; it did not prove
  showability ordering, and no mutation could, because the code does not implement it. In the
  composed graph the ports-unconfigured case is unreachable (Bootstrap configures the router ports
  first and returns early on failure), so this is a claim defect rather than a shipping defect.
- THE DECLARED CAPABILITY IS CONSUMED NARROWER THAN DECLARED. is_schedule_presentation_ports_configured
  sits in PRESENTATION_ROUTER_METHODS under the comment consumed unwidened and has zero call sites in
  the coordinator. FakePresentationRouter.set_ports_configured() was written to drive it and also has

- MINOR: _launch_presentation now overloads {} three ways -- not a presentation, already showing, and
  a router that returned an empty Dictionary would be read as one of those and reported as success.
  The real SceneRouter never returns {}, so this is robustness only.
- MINOR: the retry test comment claims begin() is idempotent per completion transaction so the retry
  does not restart a running presentation, but FakePresentationPort.begin has no cache and the test
  asserts requests.size() == 2. The property is real and proved in the port and owner suites; the

coordinator (begin_stage/begin_substage are idempotent on active at DayResolutionPlan.gd:457 and

is_ready() is literally the condition begin() refuses on in both ports, so the omitted pre-check
really is redundant; and the presentation_request guard runs first, so complete_route_stage's bare
route path is genuinely untouched.

_launched_transaction starts as "" and was compared against a command's transaction_id directly, so a presentation command carrying NO transaction id matched the UN-LAUNCHED sentinel. _launch_presentation returned {}, resume() read that as nothing-to-launch, and the walk paused on await_registered_command -- reporting a presentation in progress with no scene and no timeline behind it. Refused at the CAUSE rather than the collision: guarding with _launched_transaction != "" would leave the real defect, since resume() keys _registered_history on that same id, so a blank one also makes every later completion address the wrong entry. _launch_presentation now refuses an empty transaction_id with invalid_presentation_transaction before the sentinel comparison.

title: Implement registry-backed committed Schedule and provenance seam
description: Implement the Phase-2R committed-Schedule foundation after registry parity. Own the final committed-entry schema, Day-7 source-receipt ancestry, exact Schedule snapshot/restore validation, registry-derived route projection, and the atomic facade seam that freezes a validated committed schedule into DayResolutionPlan. This task does not own the Schedule UI draft, warning queue, or desktop-board fate.
design: Begin only after dwm-p2r.16 is closed, both of its boundary commits are integrated ancestors, and every recorded issuer/DataCatalog digest matches. Consume that exact production identity issuer for invitation-source and Schedule receipt provenance. A detached validated draft and current motivation enter one prepare/commit/rollback Schedule transaction: drafting has no canonical effect; commit charges exactly one motivation per entry, creates the canonical committed aggregate and receipts, and freezes the real ordered Schedule into DayResolutionPlan. Persist committed_schedule through the source-bound v3 RunSnapshot/SaveDocument boundary. Days 1–6 retain ordered ordinary/date input; Day 7 yields only issuer-anchored Schedule provenance for the later terminal-intent owner. Empty legacy state may migrate; nonempty pre-amendment Schedule fails closed unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Exact draft-input and committed-Schedule schemas are frozen and recursively detached. The registry alone derives cost, route, effects, participants, repeatability, legal window, and source-receipt class. Candidate success implies full committed-state validity. GameState does not mutate canonical Schedule or motivation while editing; the committed facade is idempotent, rollback-safe, and passes the real ordered Schedule rather than [] into RunLifecycle/DayResolutionPlan. Top-level committed_schedule validates and restores through the Run owner; this issue creates, restores, and mutates neither ScheduleView nor warning state. gameplay.schedule_entries and loose validate_date_candidate have zero production callers and retire at this boundary. Day-7 Schedule-provenance handoff passes without a fictitious board completion, terminal intent, ending ID, or plan. Migration, restore, focused Schedule, lifecycle, snapshot, and disk-durability gates pass.

case, not an edge case. Now matched on the DURABLE markers the domain module itself writes -- a

LEGACY_ACCEPTED_STATES. Locked by test_v2_to_v3_rejects_an_invitation_accepted_earlier_and_since_resolved.

wrote v3[contacts] unconditionally, so a snapshot with contacts ABSENT or malformed had a two-key
stub INVENTED for it -- converting a previously-rejected document into an accepted one carrying a

comments.text:
TASK 6 BLOCKED ON A PLAN SELF-CONTRADICTION (2026-08-16). Found BEFORE writing any Task-6 code.
HEAD 4a73e4d39454b7ea0c115800ef3bdff947c7968c, worktree CLEAN, index empty. Nothing was changed.
Stopping here is the standing ruling: "Immediate stop on plan self-contradiction."

THE CONTRADICTION, IN THREE FACTS THAT CANNOT ALL BE TRUE

FACT 1 -- Step 6.7 (plan line 980) demands ZERO hits from this static gate:
  rg -n "schedule_entries|begin_day_resolution\([^\r\n]*\[\]|get_state_port" \
     scripts/domain/run/DayResolutionPlan.gd scripts/domain/run/RunLifecycle.gd \
     scripts/application/run/DayResolutionCoordinator.gd \
     scripts/application/run/GameStateDayResolutionPort.gd
  Plan line 983: "Expected static output: zero hits."
  The alternation contains BARE `schedule_entries`, which matches the persisted stage id
  `execute_schedule_entries` as a substring. Measured now: 13 hits across those four files, of which
  the majority are that stage id, not the transport.

FACT 2 -- Task 7 Step 7.5 (plan line 1065) says, verbatim: "Remove `execute_schedule_entries`."
  Task 7 is dwm-p2r.14, the NEXT issue. The plan therefore explicitly schedules the removal of that
  stage AFTER Task 6. Step 6.7 cannot be demanding the same removal one task earlier without making
  Step 7.5 a no-op instruction to remove something already gone.

FACT 3 -- Removing it during Task 6 would break the v3 format Task 5 just froze.
  `execute_schedule_entries` is not a local name. It is a PERSISTED stage id inside
  lifecycle.active_resolution_plan:
    * DayResolutionPlan.DAY_1_6_STAGES:8 and DAY_7_STAGES:13 declare it positionally.
    * DayResolutionPlan.from_dict:139-140 rejects any stage whose stage_id differs from the
      allowlist entry AT THAT INDEX -- so a rename makes every existing v3 save carrying an active
      plan permanently unloadable, not merely stale.
    * DayResolutionPlan:153-154 keys the "only this stage may hold substages" rule on the literal.
    * RunSnapshotSchema preloads DayResolutionPlan (:16) and carries active_resolution_plan in
      LIFECYCLE_KEYS (:29), so the id is inside the v3 snapshot surface.
  Plan 01's own Version law (line 872) states: "Plan 02 consumes v3 unchanged and creates v4."
  Changing what v3 MEANS during Task 6, with no version bump, violates that law. Task 5's boundary
  record (committed at 4a73e4d39) binds RunSnapshotSchema.gd, SaveDocumentSchema.gd and
  SaveMigrations.gd by hash; DayResolutionPlan.gd is not hashed, so the record would not go red --
  which makes this a SILENT format break, which is worse, not better.

WHERE THE 13 HITS ACTUALLY ARE (measured, so the two readings can be priced)
  DayResolutionPlan.gd    7  -- 5 are the stage id / substage rule; 2 are the create() transport
                               parameter `schedule_entries`.
  RunLifecycle.gd         2  -- both the begin_day_resolution(resolution_id, schedule_entries)
                               transport parameter and its use at :55.
  DayResolutionCoordinator.gd 2 -- the STAGE_CONTRACTS entry for the stage id (:26) and
                               get_state_port (:81).
  GameStateDayResolutionPort.gd 3 -- :96 begin_day_resolution(command_id, []) (the synthetic seed
                               Step 6.6 exists to remove), :229 the stage id, :230 the synthesized
                               {"entry_receipt_ids": []}.
  So the gate's three genuine Task-6 targets -- the transport name, the [] seed, and get_state_port
  -- account for roughly 5 hits. The remaining ~8 are the stage id that Step 7.5 owns.

THE TWO RESOLUTIONS, AND WHY THEY PRODUCE MATERIALLY DIFFERENT COMMITS

  (A) SCOPE-FAITHFUL -- treat the gate as covering the TRANSPORT, not the stage id.
      Rename the transport `schedule_entries` -> `committed_schedule` in
      RunLifecycle.begin_day_resolution and DayResolutionPlan.create, delete get_state_port, delete
      the `[]` seed at GameStateDayResolutionPort:96 and the synthesized entry_receipt_ids at :230.
      Leave `execute_schedule_entries` alone for Step 7.5.
      Consequence: the literal rg still reports the stage-id hits, so Step 6.7's "zero hits" is NOT
      met literally and must be recorded as a deviation discharged at Task 7 Step 7.5.
      v3 stays intact. Task 6 stays inside its declared file list.
      This is consistent with plan line 983's own gloss -- "The accepted transport names
      committed_schedule explicitly" -- which talks about the TRANSPORT, not the stage vocabulary.

  (B) LITERAL -- reach zero hits now.
      Requires removing/renaming `execute_schedule_entries` during Task 6. That pulls Task 7 Step
      7.5 forward, changes the persisted plan vocabulary, breaks from_dict for any existing v3
      active plan, and contradicts the Version law. It also expands Task 6 past its declared files
      into Task 7's charter.

  RECOMMENDATION: (A). It is the only reading under which both Step 6.7 and Step 7.5 can be true,
  and the only one that leaves v3 meaning what the just-committed boundary record says it means.

  WHY THIS IS NOT SELF-RESOLVING, AND WHY I DID NOT JUST PICK (A):
  The precedent cuts the other way. At Step 5.10 the recorded decision was to follow the LITERAL
  command over the prose. Here the literal is ACHIEVABLE but only by breaking a freeze, so the
  earlier precedent does not transfer, and guessing would silently commit a save-format change
  under a subject line that promises only flow work. This is exactly the class the ruling names.

WHAT IS UNAFFECTED
  Commit 2 (4a73e4d39) is complete, verified, and independent of this question. The boundary record
  hashes only RunSnapshotSchema.gd, SaveDocumentSchema.gd and SaveMigrations.gd, none of which are
  in the disputed set. Nothing needs redoing whichever way this is resolved.

TO UNBLOCK, the next session needs ONE ruling: (A) or (B). Everything else in the Task 6 entry
survey (previous comment) stands and is ready to execute the moment that ruling exists.

title: A replayed substage completion never reports duplicate_transaction
description:
FOUND BY the fresh-context review of the dwm-p2r.20 fix plan.

THE GAP. The duplicate scan in prepare_completion walks active_resolution_plan[stages] and never
stage[substages]. A replayed SUBSTAGE completion therefore never reports duplicate: true. It falls
through to complete_active_stage, where _complete_record returns duplicate_transaction_conflict on a
differing receipt and a bare ok on an identical one.

CONSEQUENCE. A replayed substage returns stage_completed with a FRESH checkpoint rather than
duplicate_transaction. Every other seam in the coordinator is replay-idempotent and reports the
duplicate; substages silently are not. Present in the production port and mirrored in
tests/support/FakeDayResolutionStatePort.gd, so the fake would lie to any test that exercised it.

SCOPE NOTE. The dwm-p2r.20 tests deliberately avoid the duplicate path for exactly this reason.

ACCEPTANCE. The duplicate scan considers substages, so a replayed substage completion reports
duplicate_transaction and writes no second checkpoint, matching stage behaviour. RED proves the
current fall-through first. Fix the fake in the same change, or the unit suite cannot hold the claim.

REFERENCE. docs/superpowers/notes/2026-08-20-p2r20-substage-contract-through-the-route-door.md
close_reason: Closed

title: Carry contacts through the Minesweeper round transaction so group activation can commit
description:
Discovered 2026-08-17 while closing dwm-p2r.9 Step 2.5 coverage gaps on branch codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed.

Plan 06 Task 2 Step 2.4 item 7 requires the completion transaction to pass exact before/after round counts to ContactInvitationState so that only a 2->3 transition on Day 2/6 activates the group offer. That cannot happen today, and the cause is structural rather than a missing call.

GameState._SAVE_WHITELIST (autoload/GameState.gd:78-95) does NOT include the 'contacts' section. Consequences, both independently fatal:

1. GameStateMinesweeperPort._detached_clone() rebuilds its clone via reset_game() + apply_save_dict(to_save_dict()). Because to_save_dict() omits contacts, the clone always starts from DEFAULT contacts, so prepare_activate_group_after_round()'s 'both pair solos unread and AVAILABLE' predicate fails with missing_solo and never activates.
2. The port's candidate is exactly clone.to_save_dict(), which also omits contacts, so even a successful activation could never reach the committed candidate.

Verified empirically by probe on 2026-08-17: 'to_save_dict has contacts? false', 'candidate has contacts? false', receipt.group_activation_transaction_id = null, live group_action state after prepare = INACTIVE.

Therefore the hardcoded receipt values group_activation_transaction_id=null and message_transaction_ids=[] in GameStateMinesweeperPort.prepare_complete are TRUTHFUL for the current candidate surface. This is not a receipt-reporting bug; do not 'fix' it by populating those fields while contacts remain outside the transaction, or the receipt will claim a state change that was never committed.

Note that GameState._bridge_maybe_activate_group() (autoload/GameState.gd:750-763) IS correctly implemented and DOES activate on the live object with transaction id 'gactivate:day<N>'. Only the Minesweeper round transaction path cannot reach it.

dwm-p2r.9 deliberately closed without this. The plan's own rule is that only fake ports exercise this transport in .9, and the coordinator/dating contract coverage added on 2026-08-17 (139/139 gate) stands independently.
design: Widen the Minesweeper round transaction's candidate/commit/rollback surface to carry the contacts section alongside gameplay, mirroring how capture_live_run_state() and capture_restore_backup() already treat contacts as a sibling section. Then populate CompletionReceipt.group_activation_transaction_id and message_transaction_ids from the transactions the domain actually recorded, by diffing contacts.transaction_receipts on the clone and classifying new entries by their 'kind' field ('activate_group' vs 'offer_solo') rather than re-deriving the activation rule in the port. Changing the committed candidate shape touches RunSnapshotSchema and the save/restore path, so expect migration and snapshot-validation work; it also invalidates evidence/phase_2r/handoff/minesweeper_contract.json and requires regenerating both handoff artifacts and their seven-record ledger.
acceptance_criteria: Completing the third app round on an eligible Day 2 (and Day 6) commits group_action state AVAILABLE_UNOPENED with a null inviter_id and history_generated=false, and the CompletionReceipt reports the matching gactivate transaction id. Transitions 1->2 and 3->4, non-window days, and ineligible or already-read solo offers all commit no activation and report null. Dating rounds never activate the group under any transition. Both handoff artifacts and the command ledger are regenerated and validate clean.

title: Choose narrative localization adapter after representative files exist
description:
## Rationale

Only English Dialogic timelines physically exist, while the user will supply already-localized narrative files later. Choosing an adapter before one representative source/translation set exists would assume an unknown physical format and could damage stable IDs, branches, or Dialogic round trips. Affected requirement: req.locale.narrative_deferred. This decision blocks translated narrative import only; it does not block Phase 2R UI localization or English narrative validation.

## Alternatives Considered

- Godot TranslationServer resources: rejected because the approved architecture uses the user's own localized files and custom JSON for UI localization.
- Preselect a duplicated-Dialogic-timeline adapter now: rejected until physical translated files prove their structure and stable-ID behavior.
- Test at least two adapters against representative files, then record the evidence-backed choice: selected decision process.

## Decision Trigger

Reopen active work when one representative English source and corresponding external localized files are present. Inspect their formats, stable IDs, branches, and round-trip requirements before proposing the adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Representative source and translated files are present; at least two viable adapters are tested against them; the chosen adapter preserves stable IDs, branches, and Dialogic structure without inventing prose; the decision packet records evidence and closes this issue.

title: Dating rounds cannot begin during the deferred-pair presentation (stage-level route, no substage)
description: FOUND BY the dwm-p2r.23 fresh-context review, 2026-08-21, verified in source at 32416d7f4. The dwm-p2r.23 fix makes _resolve_dating_evidence resolve the ONE active surviving_date SUBSTAGE, which covers ordinary date presentations - but the deferred PAIR presentation is a TOP-LEVEL STAGE (twofriends_if_deferred, route "dating", a real paused presentation via _deferred_pair_site), during which the one active record is the stage itself, not any surviving_date: substage. A dating-context Minesweeper round attempted during the deferred-pair presentation therefore still fails DATING_ROUTE_NOT_ACTIVE - the same unbeginnable-round bug dwm-p2r.23 fixed, one door over. WHETHER IT MATTERS depends on design intent: if the deferred pair presentation can host boards (its timeline id is dating.twofriends...pre_challenge, which suggests it can), the resolver needs a stage-level branch deriving evidence from the deferred pair entry (the committed group entry Hospital superseded, participants priscilla+lavinia); if pair presentations never host boards, that must be recorded deliberately. ACCEPTANCE: decide with the design authority; if boards are hosted, RED first over the real port with a deferred-pair pause (the matrix suite's group-seed machinery reaches it); either way the resolver's docstring states which presentations can begin rounds.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:

THE COLD REVIEW, its ninth catch in nine cycles, approved the no-change disposition but found THREE real errors in my analysis, all corrected before anything landed:
E1 - my "reachable only by a port-direct caller that discards the honest receipt" claim was FALSE: the coordinator ITSELF opens the ACTIVE window through its checkpoint-failure path - resume() begins the stage on the live lifecycle, and when _commit_completion's checkpoint prepare/commit fails the begin is deliberately NOT rolled back, leaving a required=false Hospital active and unreceipted with no honest receipt ever held by the caller. The true claim, kept: no production code path ever SETTLES that window wrongly on its own (complete_route_stage answers unknown_transaction for unregistered immediate transactions; complete_presentation_stage requires _awaiting). The pin's docstring now names BOTH openings.
E2 - "no durable evidence exists" was OVERBROAD: durable condition truth DOES exist - the previous stage checkpoint's gameplay bundle carries pending_hospital in the same document as the plan (the dwm-p2r.19 guarantee), immune to the mid-presentation clear. It is dismissed on COST, now recorded as weighed-and-dismissed rather than nonexistent: the state port has no checkpoint access (the coordinator holds the checkpoint port), port-direct walks write no checkpoints at all (so refuse-when-absent would break every port-direct integration suite settling required=true hospitals), and a plan-bytes marker is a frozen-STAGE_KEYS schema migration colliding with the .25 byte laws.
E3 - my foreclosure attribution was WRONG: the resume settled-replay test drives an ACTIVE record, not a completed one. The real foreclosures of any seam state gate: the domain replay branch pinned in test_day_resolution_plan, and the coordinator's DUPLICATE path, which asks the seam BEFORE _commit_completion and therefore REQUIRES the seam to answer for already-completed records (pinned in the coordinator suite via out-of-band completion - a pin that runs against the fake's seam mirror, so production's seam-answers-completed behavior is held by fake fidelity; recorded here).

THE ANSWERED OPEN QUESTION: DesktopIdentityNonceIssuer.derive_child is a PURE derivation - it resolves the parent through read-only root captures and hashes; only issue/commit_allocation/commit_causal_day_advance/load_or_create write documents. No derivation ledger exists; a durable required-marker would be new machinery.

THE FOUR-STATE ANALYSIS, as it now stands corrected: PENDING - the mint dies at DayResolutionPlan._complete_record's stage_not_active law (:530-531), now pinned END TO END by the new test; COMPLETED + different bytes - dwm-p2r.25's duplicate_transaction_conflict (:526-529), pre-checked at prepare_completion; COMPLETED + identical - the domain's replay branch, REQUIRED behavior for the coordinator's duplicate path; ACTIVE + required=false - the one persistable window, with two openings (port-direct discard, coordinator checkpoint-failure), no production settler, and no reachable durable marker: the recorded, deliberate limit.

THE PIN, observed green on arrival twice (before and after the review's docstring amendment; 17/17, 335 asserts, zero script errors, orphans 24): the seam ANSWERS a pending hospital's transaction with the minted required=true envelope (asserted as the .28-recorded residual), and the mint then dies at the persistence door - stage_not_active, the hospital record byte-unchanged, and per the review's optional strengthening the WHOLE plan byte-identical before and after the refused landing.

With this bead resolved, the presentation settle seam's law is complete and honestly bounded: every category error is refused (.26 wrong kind, .27 superseded date, .28 wrong stage), the one state hole that can persist is characterized with both its openings and its cost-dismissed durable-marker candidates, and the doors that must stay open (completed-record answers for the duplicate path) are named with their pins.

title: prepare_completion declares a STAGE duplicate without comparing bytes, masking the conflict for stages

After the dwm-p2r.22 fix, SUBSTAGES are stricter than stages: the substage descent gates on _plan_receipt_from_envelope(receipt) == substage[receipt] and lets a mismatch fall through to the domain conflict. The fake mirrors the asymmetry deliberately (FakeDayResolutionStatePort.prepare_completion), so fixing production means fixing the fake in the same change. The descend fix as I planned it would, in that window, have handed a dating round the evidence of a date that provably never presents: the corruption class dwm-p2r.27 closed at the settle seam, reborn one seam over. title: FRIEND_IDS roster is duplicated in DataCatalog and ContactInvitationState
description:
scripts/data/DataCatalog.gd:7 and scripts/domain/contact/ContactInvitationState.gd:13 both declare FRIEND_IDS = ["priscilla", "lavinia", "sylvia"]. Two sources of truth for the same roster: adding or renaming a friend requires editing both, and nothing detects drift between them.

Pre-existing, not caused by the Plan-04 Task 4 slice, but surfaced by it: ScheduleRules now validates entry friend_ids against DataCatalog.FRIEND_IDS, which was chosen over creating a THIRD copy. Whoever does the registry parity work (dwm-wks) will hit this first.
acceptance_criteria: One canonical friend roster; the duplicate is deleted and its consumers point at the canonical constant.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Siuuuers
comments.text:
FACTS RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-21 at c3c83aabc during the overnight queue run; the bead's premises have drifted and the work is deliberately NOT done on them.

1. There are now THREE copies, not two: scripts/data/DataCatalog.gd:16, scripts/domain/contact/ContactInvitationState.gd:17, and autoload/GameState.gd:25 - all ["priscilla", "lavinia", "sylvia"]. The GameState copy has its own internal consumers (:235, :889, :971, :1114 and more).
2. The bead's canonical-choice rationale is stale: ScheduleRules does NOT validate friend_ids against DataCatalog - its header says "This module never reads DataCatalog" (the registry is injected), and a repo-wide grep finds NO consumer of DataCatalog.FRIEND_IDS outside DataCatalog itself. Every copy is internally consumed only; nothing detects drift between any pair.
3. Mechanics verified for whenever the direction is chosen: no preload cycle exists in either direction (DataCatalog preloads shop/schedule registries and StrictJson, none of which reach ContactInvitationState); ContactInvitationState.FRIEND_IDS has NO external consumers, so its copy can be re-pointed without touching callers; _has_exact_keys takes an untyped Array so the Array[String]-vs-Array typing difference is not load-bearing at the call sites checked.
4. The DIRECTION is now a design decision, not a dedup: DataCatalog's own philosophy ("registries OWN their facts; this catalog stores none of them and keeps only derived presentation") argues the roster's owner should be a DOMAIN module with data and autoload aliasing it - the OPPOSITE of the bead's original instruction - and any choice now touches the GameState autoload. That choice belongs to the maintainer; an overnight autonomous run does not make it on stale premises.

Left OPEN with acceptance unchanged. When direction is chosen, the shape is small: one canonical declaration, two aliases via path-preload (per DECISION 9.18's headless class-cache rule), plus a drift pin asserting the aliases are the canonical object.
